sec17-card-sec17-F32.front: Which six road-surface hazards routinely prompt a motorcyclist to shift position inside the lane?
sec17-card-sec17-F32.expected_back: Expect a motorcycle to change lane position for potholes, gravel, slippery patches, pavement seams, rail crossings or grooved pavement.

sec17-card-sec17-F33.front: How does the typical travel speed of scooters and mopeds compare with full-size motorcycles?
sec17-card-sec17-F33.expected_back: Scooters and mopeds usually travel more slowly than motorcycles.

sec17-card-sec17-F34.front: More than how many crashes occur each year between passenger cars and commercial vehicles?
sec17-card-sec17-F34.expected_back: The handbook reports more than two hundred fifty thousand annual crashes between cars and commercial vehicles.

sec17-card-sec17-F35.front: In what four operational ways do commercial rigs need more margin than passenger cars?
sec17-card-sec17-F35.expected_back: Compared with cars, commercial vehicles generally maneuver less readily, have larger blind spots and need greater stopping, acceleration and turning room.

sec17-card-sec17-F36.front: In the commercial-vehicle overview, what minimum dry-road stopping distance is given for a loaded truck at fifty-five miles per hour?
sec17-card-sec17-F36.expected_back: The page’s loaded-truck example gives a stopping minimum of two hundred ninety feet at fifty-five miles per hour on a clear, dry road with good tires and adjusted brakes.

sec17-card-sec17-F37.front: At least how many feet can a large bus require to come to a stop?
sec17-card-sec17-F37.expected_back: The handbook says a bus may need at least three hundred feet to stop.

sec17-card-sec17-F38.front: Besides mirror blind spots, what other danger zones around a truck or bus count as No-Zones?
sec17-card-sec17-F38.expected_back: No Zones include both places a car disappears from view and positions so close that a truck or bus cannot maneuver or stop safely.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.front: Around which sides of a large truck or bus do blind areas exist?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.expected_back: A large truck or bus has blind areas beside, behind and in front of it.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.front: Where does a large truck's right-side blind area start, and how far back can it stretch?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.expected_back: A truck’s right blind area begins behind the cab and may extend along the truck’s full length.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.front: What must you assume whenever you cannot see a commercial driver's face in the rig's side mirror?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.expected_back: If the commercial driver’s face is not visible in the side mirror, avoid assuming the driver can see you.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.front: Why should you stay alongside a large truck or bus only long enough to complete a pass?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.expected_back: Stay beside a large vehicle only as long as needed because a lane change or swerve can create a crash.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.front: In the No-Zone stopping comparison, at least how many feet does a loaded truck take from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.expected_back: This page’s loaded-truck example gives at least three hundred thirty-five feet to stop from fifty-five miles per hour under ideal conditions with good tires and adjusted brakes.

sec17-card-sec17-R06.front: How does that loaded-truck stopping distance compare with a passenger car's stopping distance?
sec17-card-sec17-R06.expected_back: The same page describes the truck stopping example as more than one-and-a-half times a car’s stopping distance.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.front: What mirror check and speed habit apply before and after merging back ahead of a passed truck?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.expected_back: Do not cut into a large vehicle’s stopping space, and after passing wait until its whole front appears in the mirror before moving ahead and maintaining speed.

sec17-card-sec17-R08.front: Up to how far behind a large vehicle does its rear blind area reach, and what two views fail inside it?
sec17-card-sec17-R08.expected_back: A large vehicle’s rear blind area can extend up to two hundred feet, so do not follow close enough to lose its driver’s view or your view ahead.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.front: Where should you position your car when following behind a large truck?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.expected_back: Position a following vehicle where the truck driver can see it in the side mirrors.

sec17-card-sec17-R10.front: Why does the handbook advise avoiding the right lane on steep hills and past truck weigh stations?
sec17-card-sec17-R10.expected_back: The handbook describes large vehicles using the right lane around thirty-five miles per hour on steep hills and advises avoiding that lane where possible on hills and near weigh-station reentry.

sec17-card-sec17-R11.front: Why must you give extra room to a truck or bus preparing for a right turn?
sec17-card-sec17-R11.expected_back: Give a turning truck or bus room because it may swing left or use another lane before completing a right turn.

sec17-card-sec17-R12.front: Why must you never slip between the curb and a right-turning truck or bus?
sec17-card-sec17-R12.expected_back: Do not move between a right-turning large vehicle and the curb; wait until its turn is complete.

sec17-card-sec17-R13.front: Where should you position your car when meeting an oncoming semi on a two-lane highway?
sec17-card-sec17-R13.expected_back: When meeting an opposing truck, keep as far right as possible to reduce sideswipe and wind-turbulence effects.

sec17-card-sec17-R14.front: What should you do at a left turn if you cannot tell how fast an oncoming truck or bus is closing?
sec17-card-sec17-R14.expected_back: If unsure about an oncoming truck or bus’s speed, do not turn left in front of it.

sec17-card-sec17-R15.front: How does stopping behind painted white stop lines help large trucks and buses at intersections?
sec17-card-sec17-R15.expected_back: Stop behind marked stop lines to preserve the turning room they provide for large vehicles.

sec17-card-sec17-R16.front: Where must you never dart across a large vehicle's bow to make a sudden move?
sec17-card-sec17-R16.expected_back: Do not cut off a large vehicle to reach an exit, turn or narrow construction lane.

sec17-card-sec17-R17.front: How must your speed behave when merging onto a highway ahead of a truck or bus?
sec17-card-sec17-R17.expected_back: Merge with traffic speed and do not move in front of a truck or bus and then slow.

sec17-card-sec17-R18.front: Why does keeping a steady pace help a truck or bus starting from an acceleration lane?
sec17-card-sec17-R18.expected_back: A truck or bus stopped on an acceleration lane needs substantial distance to regain merging speed; steady traffic pace can help it enter without another stop.

sec17-card-sec17-R19.front: Why must you never stop or park on a runaway truck ramp or its approach?
sec17-card-sec17-R19.expected_back: Never park on a runaway truck ramp or its entrance because a vehicle unable to brake may need it.

sec17-card-sec17-R20.front: What visual sign warns of a runaway truck or bus, and how must you react?
sec17-card-sec17-R20.expected_back: Brake smoke can warn of a runaway truck or bus, so move out of its path and do not enter ahead of it.

sec17-card-sec17-R21.front: What extra precaution applies around trucks and buses inside unmarked or shifting construction zones?
sec17-card-sec17-R21.expected_back: In construction zones, signs and markings may be missing; do not pull ahead of a truck or bus and stop abruptly.

sec17-card-sec17-R22.front: How should you anticipate a transit bus making frequent curbside stops ahead?
sec17-card-sec17-R22.expected_back: Watch ahead for a bus’s frequent stops and change lanes before the stop if you need to avoid queuing behind it.

sec17-card-sec17-R23.front: Which two sudden hazards must you watch for when easing past a parked transit bus?
sec17-card-sec17-R23.expected_back: Pass a parked bus cautiously because it may reenter traffic and pedestrians or children may run in front of it.

sec17-card-sec17-R24.front: About how far can the rear end of an articulated accordion bus swing sideways on turns?
sec17-card-sec17-R24.expected_back: An articulated bus has about three feet of tail swing, so leave enough room behind it for that movement.

sec17-card-sec17-R25.front: As vehicle size climbs, what happens to blind spots, stopping room, acceleration, and pass time?
sec17-card-sec17-R25.expected_back: Larger vehicles generally have greater blind spots, require more maneuver and stopping space, and take longer to accelerate or pass.

sec17-card-sec17-R26.front: How does driving a smaller vehicle affect whether truck and bus operators spot you?
sec17-card-sec17-R26.expected_back: Smaller vehicles are harder for truck and bus drivers to see.

sec17-card-sec17-R27.front: How must you yield to an approaching emergency vehicle running lights and siren?
sec17-card-sec17-R27.expected_back: Yield to an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and a siren by moving toward the road edge without blocking an intersection.

sec17-card-sec17-R28.front: Where should you bring your car to a stop when signaled by a law-enforcement officer?
sec17-card-sec17-R28.expected_back: During a police stop, move safely and promptly to the right outside the travel lane without obstructing other traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-R29.front: Should you step out of your car to meet the officer during a traffic stop?
sec17-card-sec17-R29.expected_back: Remain in the stopped vehicle unless the officer requests otherwise.

sec17-card-sec17-R30.front: What engine, lighting, and window steps belong once pulled over for a police stop?
sec17-card-sec17-R30.expected_back: For the stop described in the handbook, turn off the engine, activate hazard lights, use interior lights at night and lower the window to communicate.

sec17-card-sec17-R31.front: What should you and your passengers do with seat belts and hands while the officer walks up?
sec17-card-sec17-R31.expected_back: Stay calm with belts fastened, ask passengers to do the same, keep hands on the wheel and minimize unnecessary movement.

sec17-card-sec17-R32.front: Which three documents may be requested, and how should you reach for them safely?
sec17-card-sec17-R32.expected_back: Provide license, insurance proof and registration when requested, first telling the officer where they are and reaching slowly with one hand kept on the wheel.

sec17-card-sec17-R33.front: How should you respond to an officer's questions, and what choice must you never make?
sec17-card-sec17-R33.expected_back: Answer the officer clearly and fully and never flee law enforcement.

sec17-card-sec17-R34.front: Below what travel speed does a rear orange-and-red reflective triangle indicate?
sec17-card-sec17-R34.expected_back: A rear fluorescent or reflective orange-and-red triangle on slow equipment indicates travel below twenty-five miles per hour.

sec17-card-sec17-R35.front: How should you approach and overtake slow-moving vehicles on the highway?
sec17-card-sec17-R35.expected_back: Approach slow vehicles cautiously and pass only when safe.

sec17-card-sec17-R36.front: What rural-road assumption must you avoid around tractors and farm equipment?
sec17-card-sec17-R36.expected_back: Watch rural roads for farm equipment crossing or traveling the highway, and do not assume its operator can hear an approaching car.

sec17-card-sec17-R37.front: Do horseback riders and animal-drawn vehicles hold legal road rights and duties?
sec17-card-sec17-R37.expected_back: Animal-drawn vehicles and horseback riders have road-use rights and must follow road rules, so pass carefully.

sec17-card-sec17-R38.front: What two loud vehicle actions must you avoid near horses on or beside the road?
sec17-card-sec17-R38.expected_back: Do not sound the horn or rev the engine near horses because frightening them can cause a crash.

sec17-card-sec17-R39.front: What sudden directional move should you anticipate from animal-drawn vehicles in farm country?
sec17-card-sec17-R39.expected_back: Expect animal-drawn vehicles to turn left into fields or driveways and watch for posted warnings of these road users.

sec18-card-sec18-F01.front: Why is driving after dark inherently riskier than daytime driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F01.expected_back: Night driving is more hazardous because the headlights limit how far ahead the driver can see.

sec18-card-sec18-F02.front: When should you run high beams at night versus switching down to low beams?
sec18-card-sec18-F02.expected_back: The handbook recommends high beams without oncoming traffic but low beams when following another vehicle.

sec18-card-sec18-F03.front: How should your beams and eyes respond when meeting oncoming headlights at night?
sec18-card-sec18-F03.expected_back: Dim for oncoming traffic and look toward the right edge if another vehicle’s high beams create glare.

sec18-card-sec18-F04.front: Why must you run low beams, plus fog lamps if equipped, in fog, rain, or falling snow?
sec18-card-sec18-F04.expected_back: Use low beams in fog, rain or snow, with fitted fog lights as available, because high-beam reflection can reduce visibility.

sec18-card-sec18-F05.front: How should you manage your gaze when approaching headlights shine toward you?
sec18-card-sec18-F05.expected_back: Avoid staring into approaching headlights and keep scanning the road ahead.

sec18-card-sec18-F06.front: What visual clues ahead and along roadsides should your night scan search for?
sec18-card-sec18-F06.expected_back: Look ahead for dark road shapes and occasionally check both edges for hazards from the sides.

sec18-card-sec18-F07.front: Why should you skip sunglasses or colored lenses at night and on overcast days?
sec18-card-sec18-F07.expected_back: Avoid tinted eyewear, including sunglasses and colored lenses, during nighttime or overcast-day driving because the tint reduces vision.

sec18-card-sec18-F08.front: At least how much time should you add to your normal following interval after dark?
sec18-card-sec18-F08.expected_back: For night driving, add at least one second to the following interval.

sec18-card-sec18-F09.front: How many extra following seconds does the handbook call for at night on unfamiliar roads?
sec18-card-sec18-F09.expected_back: On an unfamiliar road at night, the handbook calls for at least two additional following seconds.

sec18-card-sec18-F10.front: What three temporary traffic changes commonly appear inside a highway work zone?
sec18-card-sec18-F10.expected_back: A work zone is a roadwork area that may include closed lanes, detours or moving equipment.

sec18-card-sec18-F11.front: Roughly how many injuries happen each year in vehicle crashes inside work zones?
sec18-card-sec18-F11.expected_back: The handbook reports about forty thousand yearly injuries from work-zone vehicle crashes.

sec18-card-sec18-F12.front: What colors distinguish work-zone warning signs, and what hazards should you scan for ahead?
sec18-card-sec18-F12.expected_back: Before entering a work zone, look for workers and large vehicles along with barrels, cones and signs; its warning signs have orange backgrounds with black words or symbols.

sec18-card-sec18-F13.front: Why must you still slow down through a work zone even when no workers are on site?
sec18-card-sec18-F13.expected_back: Reduce speed in a work zone even without workers because narrow lanes and rough pavement remain hazards.

sec18-card-sec18-F14.front: What financial penalty warning accompanies posted speed limits inside work zones?
sec18-card-sec18-F14.expected_back: Obey work-zone speed signs, noting that speeding fines may be doubled.

sec18-card-sec18-F15.front: Why should you read flashing digital boards alongside standard signs approaching roadwork?
sec18-card-sec18-F15.expected_back: Watch digital work-zone messages as well as ordinary signs because they can warn of changing conditions or slow and stopped traffic.

sec18-card-sec18-F16.front: What three driving adjustments belong all the way through an active work zone?
sec18-card-sec18-F16.expected_back: In a work zone, increase following room, monitor nearby traffic and prepare to stop.

sec18-card-sec18-F17.front: How should you treat driving through a work zone at night whether crews appear or not?
sec18-card-sec18-F17.expected_back: At night in a work zone, use extra caution whether or not workers are visible.

sec18-card-sec18-F18.front: How should you adjust lane position when passing road workers or construction rigs?
sec18-card-sec18-F18.expected_back: Adjust lane position to leave room for road workers and construction vehicles.

sec18-card-sec18-F19.front: How far must you keep obeying work-zone limits and restrictions?
sec18-card-sec18-F19.expected_back: Continue following work-zone signs until reaching End Road Work.

sec18-card-sec18-F20.front: What two trip-planning habits cut stress around scheduled road construction?
sec18-card-sec18-F20.expected_back: Plan for work-zone delays by leaving early and choosing an alternative route when possible.

sec18-card-sec18-R01.front: What three adjustments should kick in as soon as the season's first winter storm hits?
sec18-card-sec18-R01.expected_back: In the first winter storm, drive slowly, leave extra following room and refresh winter-driving habits.

sec18-card-sec18-R02.front: How should your speed and steering inputs change on snow-covered or icy winter roads?
sec18-card-sec18-R02.expected_back: For the winter conditions described, the handbook advises well below the posted limit and avoiding sudden sharp turns.

sec18-card-sec18-R03.front: How does the winter-driving paragraph describe braking technique, and what system distinction does it omit there?
sec18-card-sec18-R03.expected_back: The winter paragraph recommends light braking by gentle pumping but does not distinguish ABS-equipped vehicles there.

sec18-card-sec18-R04.front: What travel choices should you weigh before heading out in winter weather, including extreme storms?
sec18-card-sec18-R04.expected_back: Allow extra winter travel time, consider another route and stay home if conditions are too poor.

sec18-card-sec18-R05.front: May you run cruise control on wet, snowy, or icy roads?
sec18-card-sec18-R05.expected_back: Never use cruise control on slippery roads.

sec18-card-sec18-R06.front: Which lights belong on in winter driving, and which setting should you skip in night snowstorms?
sec18-card-sec18-R06.expected_back: Use headlights in winter and avoid high beams during a nighttime storm to prevent glare.

sec18-card-sec18-R07.front: Does winter clothing or slow snow driving ever excuse skipping your seat belt?
sec18-card-sec18-R07.expected_back: Continue using the seatbelt in winter driving.

sec18-card-sec18-R08.front: Why must you slow down and give wide clearance to operating snowplows?
sec18-card-sec18-R08.expected_back: Slow and leave snowplows ample room because they are wide, may work near the centerline and can throw up visibility-blocking snow.

sec18-card-sec18-R09.front: How far back must you stay behind a flashing red-or-amber snowplow where the limit is thirty-five miles per hour or higher?
sec18-card-sec18-R09.expected_back: Where the posted limit is at least thirty-five miles per hour, stay at least two hundred feet behind a snowplow displaying red or amber lights.

sec18-card-sec18-R10.front: What three consequences can hit a driver who ignores closure gates and gets stuck on a closed road?
sec18-card-sec18-R10.expected_back: A driver stuck on a closed road may face delayed rescue, a ticket and responsibility for rescue-related costs for people or the vehicle.

sec18-card-sec18-R11.front: What three core habits keep you safe across open rural highways?
sec18-card-sec18-R11.expected_back: On rural roads, remain alert, watch warnings and obey speed limits while accounting for their particular hazards.

sec18-card-sec18-R12.front: How should you adjust speed and following gap when pavement turns to loose gravel or dirt?
sec18-card-sec18-R12.expected_back: On gravel or dirt, slow down and increase following room because traction is lower and stopping may cause a skid.

sec18-card-sec18-R13.front: How should you drive a narrow country road with steep drop-offs or almost no shoulder?
sec18-card-sec18-R13.expected_back: On a narrow rural road with little shoulder or a drop-off, reduce speed, center within the lane and watch for opposing vehicles encroaching.

sec18-card-sec18-R14.front: How do drivers decide who crosses a narrow or single-lane rural bridge first?
sec18-card-sec18-R14.expected_back: At a narrow or single-lane bridge, follow warning signs and take turns, with the first arriving driver generally having priority.

sec18-card-sec18-R15.front: What three steps belong on open-grate or steel rural bridge decks?
sec18-card-sec18-R15.expected_back: On open-grate or steel bridges, reduce speed, increase following space and hold the wheel firmly because grip may be reduced.

sec18-card-sec18-R16.front: How must you drive where tall corn, timber, blind bends, or steep crests block rural visibility?
sec18-card-sec18-R16.expected_back: Slow and prepare to stop where woods, crops, blind bends or steep hills limit sight distance.

sec18-card-sec18-R17.front: How should you approach an uncontrolled rural intersection with no signs or lights?
sec18-card-sec18-R17.expected_back: At an uncontrolled rural intersection, approach cautiously, slow down and prepare to stop for crossing or opposing traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Why must you evaluate live traffic conditions instead of assuming right-of-way rules guarantee your path?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Right-of-way rules guide yielding and the order of entry, but drivers must consider the actual situation rather than assume priority automatically.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: How do you yield when another driver is already in an intersection or gets there ahead of you?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Yield to a driver already at the intersection or arriving there before you.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Who gets priority when you want to turn left across an opposing lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: When turning left, yield to traffic approaching in the opposite lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: Who yields when two drivers reach an all-way stop at the exact same time?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: At an all-way stop, drivers who arrive simultaneously must yield to the driver on the right.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: Who must yield when a vehicle pulls onto a public highway from a private road or driveway?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: When entering a public highway from a driveway or private road, yield to highway traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: Who has the duty to yield where an entrance or acceleration ramp meets an interstate highway?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: A driver on an entrance or acceleration ramp must yield to vehicles already on the limited-access or interstate highway.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: Which three groups still inside an intersection must receive right-of-way before you enter?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers still within the intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Which vehicle in a South Dakota funeral procession must obey traffic signs and signals?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: The funeral-procession rule says only its first vehicle must obey traffic signs and signals.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: How do funeral-procession cars mark themselves, and what must surrounding motorists avoid doing?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Vehicles in a funeral procession must use their headlights, and other drivers must not cut into or interfere with the procession.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Besides signs, signals, and lane paint, which three groups of people direct traffic as official controls?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Traffic-control devices include signals, signs, road markings and directions from police, highway workers and school crossing guards.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: Where are pedestrian hybrid beacons installed to help walkers cross safely?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: A pedestrian hybrid beacon helps people cross busy or faster roads at midblock crossings and uncontrolled intersections.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: How many red and yellow lenses make up the pedestrian hybrid beacon described in the handbook?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: The pedestrian hybrid beacon described in the handbook has two red lenses above one yellow lens.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: How does a pedestrian hybrid beacon appear before a walker presses the crossing button?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: A pedestrian hybrid beacon stays dark until a pedestrian presses the call button.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: What color progression directs motorists to slow and stop once a pedestrian activates a hybrid beacon?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: After activation, the beacon follows a yellow-to-red sequence with steady and flashing lights directing motorists to slow and stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What happens on the pedestrian screen and overhead beacon as the walker finishes crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: The handbook says the pedestrian display then flashes WALK and the beacon returns dark after the pedestrian crosses safely.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: How are red, yellow, and green lenses ordered on vertical versus horizontal traffic signals?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Vertical traffic signals normally show red above yellow above green, while horizontal signals place red left, yellow center and green right.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: What must you wait for at a steady red light before driving straight through?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: A steady red signal requires a complete stop and waiting for green and clear crossing traffic before proceeding straight.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: Under what three conditions may you make a right turn at a steady red light?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: A right turn on red is allowed only after stopping completely when safe and when no sign forbids the turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Who gets right-of-way before you turn on red, and where must your car finish the turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Before turning on red, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and vehicles, then turn safely while remaining in the proper lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: Which intersection sign matches the exact rule for a flashing red traffic light?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop fully, then continue only when safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: When may you move in the direction pointed by a steady red arrow?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: A red arrow prohibits movement in its direction until it goes out and a green arrow or green light appears.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: What does a steady yellow traffic light warn, and what action does it require?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: A steady yellow light warns that red is next and requires stopping when stopping is safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: What should you do if the signal switches to yellow after your car is already inside the intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: If yellow appears after the vehicle is already in the intersection, continue through instead of stopping there.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: How should you drive through an intersection displaying a flashing yellow light?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: A flashing yellow signal calls for reduced speed and caution.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: What does a steady yellow arrow warn turning drivers to do?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: A yellow arrow means protected turning is ending, so prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: What must you do before turning left on a flashing yellow left arrow?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: A flashing yellow left arrow permits a cautious left turn only when safe after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: What signal color is oncoming traffic facing while you see a flashing yellow left arrow?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Oncoming traffic has a green signal while the described flashing-yellow left arrow is displayed.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: Does a steady green light erase your duty to yield to emergency vehicles or legally protected road users?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: A steady green permits proceeding but does not remove duties to yield to emergency vehicles and others required by law.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: What must clear out of the intersection when your red light first turns green?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: When a stopped driver receives green, crossing traffic must clear before the driver enters.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: Under what rules may you turn left at a steady circular green signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: A left turn on a steady green is allowed only when safe, with oncoming traffic having priority and any left-turn prohibition still obeyed.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: Who must you watch closely across your path during any left or right turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: During a right or left turn, watch for pedestrians crossing in front of the vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: What traffic condition is expected when a steady green arrow illuminates for your turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: A green arrow permits turning in its indicated direction, with no oncoming or crossing traffic expected during that arrow.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: How should a driver facing green proceed when a traffic signal is malfunctioning under South Dakota statute?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: When a signal malfunctions, a driver facing green may proceed cautiously under SDCL thirty-two-twenty-eight-two.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: How should a driver facing yellow proceed at a malfunctioning traffic signal under South Dakota statute?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: When a signal malfunctions, a driver facing yellow may proceed cautiously under SDCL thirty-two-twenty-eight-three.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: How must you treat a malfunctioning signal that is stuck red or completely dark?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.memory_hook: Treat dark or red as stop
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: A red or completely dark malfunctioning signal must be treated as a stop sign.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: Which four visual features help you recognize a road sign's category from a distance?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: A sign’s shape, color, symbols and wording help identify whether it communicates rules, hazards, directions, locations or services.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: What standard shape and color scheme identify most roadway warning signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Warning signs usually have a diamond shape with a yellow background and black words or symbols.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Which three pedestrian-focused warning zones often use bright fluorescent yellow signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Some school-zone, school-crossing and pedestrian-crossing warnings use fluorescent yellow.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: What do warning signs announce, and how should your driving adjust?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: A warning sign announces possible danger or a special road situation and may require slowing or preparing to stop.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: What shape and markings warn in advance of a railroad crossing, and what four actions follow?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.memory_hook: Round yellow sign, slow, look, listen
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Before a rail crossing, a round yellow sign with an X and black RR letters warns drivers to slow, look, listen and prepare to stop for an approaching train.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: What white X-shaped sign stands right beside the tracks at a highway-rail crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: A white X-shaped crossbuck marked Railroad Crossing stands at the highway-rail intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: Where must you stop at a crossbuck crossing when a train or rail vehicle approaches?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: At a crossbuck crossing, an approaching train or rail vehicle requires stopping behind the stop line or before the intersection is clear.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: What hidden danger does a multiple-track sign warn about below a crossbuck?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: A multiple-track sign warns that another track and another train may be present.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: Why must you scan carefully for extra tracks and trains at every rail crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.memory_hook: Some crossings lack signs or lights
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: Always check for additional tracks and trains because some multiple-track crossings lack the number-of-tracks sign and some crossings have no lights.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: What action is mandatory whenever rail-crossing red lights flash alternately?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: Alternately flashing rail-crossing lights require a stop.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: May you ever weave around a lowered railroad crossing gate if no train is visible?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Never drive around a lowered rail-crossing gate.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: When a railroad crossing bell or horn is sounding, when is it lawful to cross?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: Where a rail-crossing bell or horn sounds, do not cross until the warning sound stops.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: What vital contact information appears on the railroad Emergency Notification System sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: The railroad emergency-notification sign provides a dispatch phone number for reporting crossing, track or train problems.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: What color sign displays the emergency notification phone number at a railroad crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: The emergency-notification number is generally on a blue sign at or near the crossing.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: What does the Department of Transportation code on the blue railroad sign identify?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: The same sign’s DOT number identifies the crossing location for emergency crews and railroad staff.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: Why must you read off the Department of Transportation crossing identifier when calling railroad dispatch?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: Give the crossing’s DOT identifier when reporting trouble so dispatch can identify it and warn or slow approaching trains.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.front: What color and shapes distinguish temporary work-zone signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.memory_hook: Orange diamonds or rectangles, black print
sec09-card-sec09-R17.expected_back: Work-zone signs are generally orange with black markings and have diamond or rectangular shapes.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.front: Which five roadway changes do orange work-zone signs commonly announce?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.memory_hook: Workers, lower speeds, detours, gear, surfaces
sec09-card-sec09-R18.expected_back: Work-zone warnings may announce workers, lower speeds, detours, slow equipment or changing road surfaces.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.front: How must you respond to a work-zone flagger's paddle sign or flag directions?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.expected_back: Obey a work-zone controller’s signs or flags directing travel, slowing or stopping.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.front: What job do orange drums, cones, vertical panels, and barricades perform in a work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.expected_back: Work-zone drums, cones, panels and barricades guide traffic away from hazardous or closed areas.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.front: Where must you halt when stopping for a temporary portable traffic signal in a work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.expected_back: Temporary work-zone signals may be used, and a driver stopping there must stop at a white line when one is present.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.front: What three driving adjustments keep you crash-free through an active work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.expected_back: In a work zone, slow down, expect sudden stops and avoid following too closely.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.front: What happens to speeding fines inside a South Dakota highway work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.expected_back: Speeding fines in a work zone may be doubled.

sec09-card-sec09-R24.front: What types of enforceable rules do regulatory signs communicate?
sec09-card-sec09-R24.memory_hook: Enforceable speed, turn, lane, parking laws
sec09-card-sec09-R24.expected_back: Regulatory signs communicate laws for direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking and other situations that drivers must obey.

sec09-card-sec09-R25.front: What background color, marking colors, and shapes characterize regulatory signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R25.expected_back: Regulatory signs are white with black, red or green markings and may be square, rectangular or specially shaped.

sec09-card-sec09-R26.front: What does a red circle with a diagonal slash drawn across a black symbol mean?
sec09-card-sec09-R26.expected_back: A red circle and slash over a regulatory symbol prohibit the action represented.

sec09-card-sec09-R27.front: Which two speed boundaries can black-and-white regulatory speed signs establish?
sec09-card-sec09-R27.expected_back: Black-and-white speed signs state the maximum permitted speed or a required minimum.

sec09-card-sec09-R28.front: When is driving the full posted maximum speed appropriate, and when must you drop below it?
sec09-card-sec09-R28.expected_back: Use the posted maximum only in ideal conditions and reduce speed for slippery roads, precipitation, ice or limited visibility.

sec09-card-sec09-R29.front: What should you do if conditions or your vehicle keep you from safely matching a road's posted minimum speed?
sec09-card-sec09-R29.expected_back: On a road with a minimum speed, use another road if that posted minimum is too fast for you.

sec09-card-sec09-R30.front: What unique shape and color combination belongs exclusively to a stop sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R30.expected_back: A stop sign is red with white lettering and has eight sides.

sec09-card-sec09-R31.front: In South Dakota's regulatory sign rules, where do you stop at a stop sign and what follows?
sec09-card-sec09-R31.expected_back: At a stop sign, stop behind an existing stop line or crosswalk, or before the sign when neither is present, then check every direction and yield.

sec09-card-sec09-R32.front: What shape, orientation, and colors identify a standard yield sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R32.expected_back: A yield sign is a downward-pointing red-and-white triangle with red lettering.

sec09-card-sec09-R33.front: What must you do as you approach a yield sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R33.expected_back: A yield sign requires slowing and giving priority to traffic in the intersection or road being entered.

sec09-card-sec09-R34.front: How must you travel when entering or driving along a street marked with one-way signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R34.expected_back: On a one-way street, travel only in the arrow’s direction and never turn or drive against it.

sec09-card-sec09-R35.front: How do roads mark where legal passing starts, ends, or stays off-limits?
sec09-card-sec09-R35.expected_back: No-passing signs and pavement markings identify passing-zone beginnings and endings and places where passing is prohibited.

sec09-card-sec09-R36.front: What sightline factors and hidden features determine where engineers place no-passing zones?
sec09-card-sec09-R36.expected_back: Passing-zone placement considers visible distance and hidden hazards such as hills, curves, intersections and driveways.

sec09-card-sec09-R37.front: Does a broken yellow passing zone mean it is automatically safe to pull out and overtake?
sec09-card-sec09-R37.expected_back: Even where passing is permitted, pass only when safe in the actual road and traffic conditions.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: What must you scan at every corner and activate before starting a turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Before a turn, scan every corner for controls, pedestrians and vehicles, and signal the intended movement.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Which lane position should you enter and hold when preparing to turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Enter and hold the lane position nearest the intended turn direction.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: How far along your intended turning path should you aim your eyes?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Look as far along the intended turning path as possible.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: What three steps finish a turn cleanly once your wheels straighten?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: After turning, accelerate smoothly to an appropriate speed, confirm the signal has cancelled and check behind.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: From where in your lane do you start a right turn, and what steering habit must you avoid?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Start a right turn from the lane’s rightmost portion without first swinging left.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: Where in your lane do you begin a left turn, and who holds priority?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Start a left turn from the lane’s leftmost portion and yield to oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: How must you handle lane selection when two or more lanes turn together?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Where several lanes turn, choose the turn lane beforehand and remain in it until the turn is finished.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: How does a two-point turnabout reverse your direction when circling the block isn't practical?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: A two-point turnabout uses a street, alley or driveway to reverse direction when going around the block is impractical or impossible.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: What three initial actions start a reverse two-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Begin a reverse two-point turnabout with a right signal, a stop and side-and-rear traffic checks.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: When do you turn the steering wheel fully right while backing into a reverse two-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: For that reverse turnabout, back until the rear bumper reaches the driveway’s near edge, then back slowly while steering fully right.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: What do you do with steering and brakes once your car backs into the driveway?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: As the vehicle enters the driveway during the reverse turnabout, straighten the wheels and stop.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: How do you complete a reverse two-point turnabout from inside the driveway?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Finish the reverse turnabout by selecting Drive, checking both directions and, when clear, signaling and turning left into the proper lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: How do you position and signal to start a forward two-point turnabout into a left driveway?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: Begin a forward two-point turnabout by checking mirrors, signaling left and approaching near the road center before entering the driveway or alley near its right side.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: Where do you stop inside the driveway during a forward two-point turnabout before shifting to Reverse?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: In that forward turnabout, stop when the rear clears the curb or driveway edge, then check every direction, signal right and select Reverse.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: How do you steer, shift, and finish backing out of a forward two-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: With the path clear, reverse slowly while steering fully right; on entering the nearest lane, straighten, stop, select Drive, cancel the right signal and proceed.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: When is a three-point turnabout appropriate to use?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Use a three-point turnabout only on a two-lane road too narrow for a U-turn when going around the block is impossible.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: What three steps begin a three-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Begin a three-point turnabout by checking mirrors, signaling right and stopping along the road’s right side.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: How do you execute the first forward crossing of a three-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: For its first crossing, signal left, check traffic and the left-shoulder blind spot, and once traffic is clear steer sharply left across the roadway and stop upon reaching the far side.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: How do you perform the middle reversing stage of a three-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: For the reversing stage, select Reverse, check traffic and both blind spots, then turn sharply right and stop on the opposite side when clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: What checks and signals accompany the final forward turn of a three-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: For the final stage, select Drive, signal left, check traffic and blind spots, then turn left into the right-hand lane in the new direction when clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: What final checks follow completing a three-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: After completing the three-point turnabout, check traffic, confirm signal cancellation and continue straight in the new direction.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: How does a U-turn reverse your direction compared with multi-point turnabouts?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: A U-turn reverses travel direction in a single smooth U-shaped movement within the road.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: When may you make a U-turn at an intersection directed by a police officer?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: Do not U-turn at a police-controlled intersection unless the officer directs it.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: Where are midblock U-turns prohibited in South Dakota, and what divided-road exception exists?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: Midblock U-turns are prohibited on a business-district street or a residential through highway, except at a legal opening or crossover on a divided road.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: May you make a U-turn where a No U-Turn regulatory sign is posted?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: Do not make a U-turn where a sign prohibits it.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: What minimum sight distance from all directions is required for a U-turn near a curve or hillcrest on an undivided highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: On an undivided highway near a curve or hillcrest, do not U-turn where an approaching driver in any direction cannot see the vehicle from five hundred feet away.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: What general safety test governs every otherwise legal U-turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: Do not U-turn when the maneuver cannot be completed safely without interfering with traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: What speed adjustment and six visual checks apply as you approach an intersection?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: At intersections, reduce speed and scan controls, opposing and crossing traffic, pedestrians, bicycles, road conditions and limited-view areas.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: Why shouldn't you count on cross-street drivers obeying signs, signals, or yield rules?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: Do not assume other road users will obey signs or signals or yield; be ready to avoid a crash.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: What scanning sequence should you use for cross traffic and bicycles after stopping at an intersection?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: Before entering after an intersection stop, check crossing traffic and bicycles, using the recommended left-right-left scan.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: Why shouldn't you floor the gas the instant a red light turns green?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: A green light is not a reason to start immediately without checking that crossing traffic has cleared.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: How big must your traffic gap be when crossing or turning onto a cross street?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: Choose a gap large enough to cross, reach the proper turn lane and accelerate without assuming another driver will make room.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: Why shouldn't you pull out solely because an approaching car has its turn signal flashing?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: Do not enter merely because an approaching driver signals a turn; that driver may turn farther ahead or have left the signal on.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: Which way does traffic circulate inside a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: Roundabout traffic circulates one way counterclockwise.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: By roughly what percentages do roundabouts cut fatal crashes, injury crashes, and total crashes?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: The handbook reports approximate roundabout crash reductions of ninety percent for fatalities, seventy-five percent for injuries and thirty-five percent overall compared with other intersection controls.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: What is a roundabout's inner truck apron built for, and which vehicles must stay off it?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: A truck apron is the paved inner roundabout area for large trucks’ rear wheels during turns, and cars, SUVs and pickups must not use it.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How should you manage speed, signs, walkers, and cyclists when approaching a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Approach a roundabout slowly, obey its signs and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Which direction do you check for priority vehicles before entering a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Yield to traffic already circulating on the left and enter a roundabout only through a safe gap.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: What speed rule applies while driving inside a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: Keep speed low inside a roundabout.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: What signal and yield duties apply as your roundabout exit approaches?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Signal right as the roundabout exit approaches and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists while leaving.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: Who always holds priority when emergency sirens approach a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Always yield to emergency vehicles at a roundabout.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches before you enter a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: If an emergency vehicle approaches before you enter the roundabout, pull over and let it pass.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already circulating inside a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: If already inside the roundabout, continue to the exit before pulling over for an emergency vehicle and avoid stopping within the circle.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: How do you choose the proper lane before entering a multilane roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Before entering a multilane roundabout, follow the roadside signs and pavement arrows to select the correct lane.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: Which lane is generally used to turn left at a multilane roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: For a left turn at a multilane roundabout, generally use the left lane or another lane specifically signed and marked for left turns.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: Which lane is generally used to turn right at a multilane roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: For a right turn at a multilane roundabout, generally use the right lane or another lane specifically signed and marked for right turns.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: Which lane should you pick when continuing straight through a multilane roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: For straight travel through a multilane roundabout, use the lane indicated by the signs and arrows.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: What traffic movements require special attention at a cloverleaf highway interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: At a cloverleaf interchange, watch for vehicles entering or leaving the highway.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.front: What conflict happens inside cloverleaf weaving sections between loop ramps?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.expected_back: Cloverleaf weaving areas can put entering and exiting traffic together in the short freeway sections between loop ramps.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.front: Why must you shed substantial speed on cloverleaf loop ramps?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.expected_back: Cloverleaf ramp loops often require a much lower speed for their curves.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.front: Which three interchange designs avoid cloverleaf weaving conflicts?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.expected_back: The handbook contrasts cloverleaf weaving issues with diamond, diverging-diamond and single-point urban interchange alternatives.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.front: Do ordinary intersection traffic rules still apply inside a diverging-diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.expected_back: General intersection rules still apply when driving a diverging-diamond interchange.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.front: How should you navigate the first signalized crossover of a diverging-diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.expected_back: At the first DDI signal set, follow the signs, signals and road markings through the crossing, where traffic appears to move like a one-way street.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.front: Why are left turns onto the freeway effortless inside a diverging-diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.expected_back: The handbook’s DDI description calls left turns onto the freeway free-flow movements without a stop to enter the ramp.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.front: What does a driver traveling straight across a diverging-diamond interchange encounter at the far end?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.expected_back: A driver going straight through the described DDI passes a second set of traffic signals.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.front: Where must pedestrians walk and cross inside a diverging-diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.expected_back: Pedestrians in a DDI use designated walkways and cross only at crosswalks.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.front: Which two routing options may bicyclists use through a diverging-diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.expected_back: A bicyclist in the described DDI may use a bike lane or the pedestrian walkways and crosswalks.

sec11-card-sec11-R22.front: May a motorist drive across an interstate highway's center median?
sec11-card-sec11-R22.expected_back: Do not cross an interstate highway’s median.

sec11-card-sec11-R23.front: What must you do if you overshoot your intended exit on an interstate?
sec11-card-sec11-R23.expected_back: If an interstate exit is missed, continue to the next exit and never back up on the interstate.

sec11-card-sec11-R24.front: Which interstate lane habit applies when you are not overtaking slower traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-R24.expected_back: Avoid unnecessary interstate lane changes and stay right unless overtaking and passing another vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-R25.front: How should you manage your cruising pace on an interstate highway?
sec11-card-sec11-R25.expected_back: On an interstate, maintain a steady pace with traffic while obeying posted speed limits.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: Which two vehicle categories require a South Dakota driver license when operated on public roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Riders sometimes assume small motor-driven cycles dodge licensing rules, yet public roadways require a driver license for both.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: Within how many days after establishing residency must a valid out-of-state noncommercial license holder apply in South Dakota?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Letting your home-state card ride past ninety days leaves a new resident driving past South Dakota's transfer deadline.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: At what minimum age may a nonresident drive in South Dakota using a valid home-state operator license?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Even though local teens start permits at fourteen, visiting out-of-state drivers must be at least sixteen with valid home licensing.
sec02-card-sec02-F03.must_match_memory_hook: Nonresidents sixteen up with home license

visual_sync.text_span: Nonresidents sixteen up with home license

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: Where must your driver license be kept whenever you are operating a motor vehicle in South Dakota?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Memorizing your license number will not satisfy a traffic stop if the physical credential is not in your possession.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: What is the minimum age stated in the handbook for obtaining a South Dakota driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: South Dakota features one of the nation's earliest entry ages, making fourteen a classic written-exam number to lock down.
sec02-card-sec02-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Minimum South Dakota age is fourteen

visual_sync.text_span: Minimum South Dakota age is fourteen

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Whose consent is required on every driver-license application submitted by someone younger than eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Consent applies to every application while under eighteen, not merely the initial instruction permit visit.
sec02-card-sec02-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Under eighteen needs parent or guardian

visual_sync.text_span: Under eighteen needs parent or guardian

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: What two general requirements must every South Dakota driver-license applicant satisfy for their specific application?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Passing exams without proper paperwork—or bringing paperwork without passing required exams—stalls your credential at the counter.
sec02-card-sec02-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Bring required documents, pass applicable tests

visual_sync.text_span: Bring required documents, pass applicable tests

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: What must an applicant do with existing driver licenses and identification cards when obtaining a South Dakota driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Examiners collect both old driver licenses and state identification cards so no applicant keeps duplicate credentials.
sec02-card-sec02-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Surrender existing licenses and ID cards

visual_sync.text_span: Surrender existing licenses and ID cards

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: How do active suspensions, revocations, or denials in South Dakota or another state affect license eligibility?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Moving across state lines never clears a blocked driving record because interstate checks block licensing during any active sanction.
sec02-card-sec02-F09.must_match_memory_hook: No active suspension, revocation, or denial

visual_sync.text_span: No active suspension, revocation, or denial

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: Which three court findings disqualify a person from obtaining a South Dakota driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Notice the rule hinges on a formal court finding of mental incompetence, alcoholism, or habitual illegal drug use.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: What rule applies to unpaid fines for moving traffic violations when applying for a license?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Outstanding moving-violation fines freeze your licensing eligibility until every balance is settled.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: What immigration or presence requirement is part of South Dakota's driver-license eligibility list?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Every credential pathway in South Dakota requires verifying legal presence inside the United States before issuance.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: What specific information must USCIS documents show for an applicant from another country?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Examiners need exact authorized-stay dates from federal immigration records because those dates cap when the credential expires.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: Why should dark or tinted corrective lenses be avoided when driving at night?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Darkened lenses block scarce nighttime light from reaching your eyes right when unlit obstacles are hardest to spot.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: Why is keeping spare glasses inside your vehicle recommended?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Snapping frames or misplacing glasses away from home will not strand you illegally when a backup pair rides along.
sec05-card-sec05-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Spare glasses rescue broken or lost

visual_sync.text_span: Spare glasses rescue broken or lost

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: Which three traffic sounds can alert a driver to approaching danger?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Blasting cabin music drowns out emergency sirens, warning horns, and screeching tires before hazards enter view.
sec05-card-sec05-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Horns, sirens, and skidding tires warn

visual_sync.text_span: Horns, sirens, and skidding tires warn

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: How can a motorist who knows about hearing loss compensate safely behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Frequent mirror sweeps and sharp visual scanning catch emergency strobes and closing cars that muted ears might miss.
sec05-card-sec05-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Lean harder on vision and alertness

visual_sync.text_span: Lean harder on vision and alertness

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: How do the driving records of hearing-impaired motorists compare with those of drivers who hear well?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Consistent visual scanning lets drivers with hearing loss maintain safety records equal to motorists with full hearing.
sec05-card-sec05-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Hearing-impaired driving records match everyone else's

visual_sync.text_span: Hearing-impaired driving records match everyone else's

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: How does the handbook define fatigue, and which four triggers can bring it on?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Recognizing mental tiredness alongside physical exhaustion stops drivers from assuming only late bedtimes create highway drowsiness.
sec05-card-sec05-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Exertion, repetition, illness, or short sleep

visual_sync.text_span: Exertion, repetition, illness, or short sleep

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: Which two driving abilities suffer under fatigue, and what does the handbook advise when you are tired?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Blurry sight paired with sluggish choices stretches stopping distance dramatically, so staying off the road beats pushing through.
sec05-card-sec05-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Impairs vision, slows decisions, skip driving

visual_sync.text_span: Impairs vision, slows decisions, skip driving

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: How many hours of sleep do most people need before a trip to stay alert during the day?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Starting a highway haul on four or five hours of sleep invites highway hypnosis well before sunset.
sec05-card-sec05-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Seven to nine hours builds alertness

visual_sync.text_span: Seven to nine hours builds alertness

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: How often—by distance or driving time—should trip planning schedule rest stops?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Stepping out before drowsiness hits resets circulation and focus far better than grinding nonstop across state highways.
sec05-card-sec05-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Stop every hundred miles, two hours

visual_sync.text_span: Stop every hundred miles, two hours

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: How can a travel companion help guard against drowsy driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: An awake passenger often notices lane drifting or heavy eyelids before a tired driver admits losing focus.
sec05-card-sec05-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Companions watch how you are driving

visual_sync.text_span: Companions watch how you are driving

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: What should you look for on medicine labels before getting behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Everyday allergy or cold tablets can trigger sudden highway sleepiness if you skip reading the warning panel.
sec05-card-sec05-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Check medicine labels for drowsiness warnings

visual_sync.text_span: Check medicine labels for drowsiness warnings

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: What does the fatigue section advise regarding alcohol or drug use when driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Depressants and impairing substances compound tiredness rapidly and wreck reaction timing behind the wheel.
sec05-card-sec05-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Never mix alcohol or drugs driving

visual_sync.text_span: Never mix alcohol or drugs driving

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: What should you do right away—and for how long if napping—when you start feeling tired on the road?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Rolling down windows never cures sleep debt, whereas pulling off for a brief power nap or room saves lives.
sec05-card-sec05-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Exit for fifteen-to-twenty-minute nap or lodging

visual_sync.text_span: Exit for fifteen-to-twenty-minute nap or lodging

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: When does the handbook suggest taking caffeine relative to a short roadside nap?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Drinking caffeine just before closing your eyes lets both alertness boosts kick in together as you wake.
sec05-card-sec05-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Drink caffeine right before short naps

visual_sync.text_span: Drink caffeine right before short naps

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Which two broad habits are the handbook's core recommendations for preventing driver fatigue?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Respecting your body's overnight sleep clock and resting fully beforehand beat every emergency wake-up trick.
sec05-card-sec05-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Skip late-night driving, get plenty rest

visual_sync.text_span: Skip late-night driving, get plenty rest

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: How does the handbook define distraction, even when your eyes stay forward and hands stay on the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Daydreaming causes inattention blindness even while staring straight through the windshield with both hands planted.
sec05-card-sec05-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Anything shifting focus, including mental drift

visual_sync.text_span: Anything shifting focus, including mental drift

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: What three crash outcomes can result from distracted driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Looking away or tuning out for a few highway lengths can end in wreckage, serious trauma, or fatalities.
sec05-card-sec05-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Injury, death, or costly property damage

visual_sync.text_span: Injury, death, or costly property damage

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Which three phone or screen activities does South Dakota state law prohibit while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Notice scrolling a message or social feed violates state law identically to typing a reply.
sec05-card-sec05-F26.must_match_memory_hook: No texting, reading messages, social apps

visual_sync.text_span: No texting, reading messages, social apps

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: Which two kinds of conversations—plus what everyday habit—should drivers avoid behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Heated debates hijack mental bandwidth while unwrapping food pulls hands off the steering wheel.
sec05-card-sec05-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Skip arguments, emotional talks, and eating

visual_sync.text_span: Skip arguments, emotional talks, and eating

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: How should children and pets be secured inside a moving vehicle to prevent distraction?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Loose pets climbing onto your lap or unbuckled kids create sudden cabin chaos and deadly crash projectiles.
sec05-card-sec05-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Restrain children, crate pets in carriers

visual_sync.text_span: Restrain children, crate pets in carriers

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: Which two permit tiers are barred from using wireless communication devices while operating a motor vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Unlike adult operators limited mainly on texting, teen permit holders cannot use wireless communication gear at all.
sec05-card-sec05-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Instruction and restricted permits ban wireless

visual_sync.text_span: Instruction and restricted permits ban wireless

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: What two fundamental duties is every motorist responsible for behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Every traffic statute ultimately rests on keeping undivided focus and handling the car safely around others.
sec05-card-sec05-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Pay full attention, operate vehicle safely

visual_sync.text_span: Pay full attention, operate vehicle safely

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: How does the handbook define aggressive driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Deliberate risk-taking separates aggressive driving from an honest mistake and puts nearby lives and vehicles in jeopardy.
sec05-card-sec05-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Intentional acts endangering people or property

visual_sync.text_span: Intentional acts endangering people or property

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: Which five on-road behaviors does the handbook list as typical examples of aggressive driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Combining excessive speed, tight following, abrupt cuts, skipped turn signals, and blown signs leaves zero room for error.
sec05-card-sec05-F32.must_match_memory_hook: Speeding, tailgating, weaving, bad signals, running

visual_sync.text_span: Speeding, tailgating, weaving, bad signals, running

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: How does the handbook advise drivers to focus and treat fellow road users?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Letting small traffic annoyances slide with patience and courtesy defuses road-rage spirals before they start.
sec05-card-sec05-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Concentrate on driving, stay patient, courteous

visual_sync.text_span: Concentrate on driving, stay patient, courteous

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: About what percentage of fatal traffic crashes each year involve alcohol or other impairing drugs?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Nearly two out of every five deadly highway wrecks trace back to alcohol or impairing drug use.
sec05-card-sec05-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Roughly forty percent of fatal crashes

visual_sync.text_span: Roughly forty percent of fatal crashes

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: How do even small amounts of alcohol or impairing drugs affect crash risk compared with sober driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Feeling buzz-free after one drink does not prevent measurable rises in collision risk compared with driving sober.
sec05-card-sec05-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Even small amounts raise crash risk

visual_sync.text_span: Even small amounts raise crash risk

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: Why does alcohol hit new drivers harder than experienced motorists?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Because novices must consciously think through steering and scanning, alcohol disrupts unpracticed habits much faster.
sec05-card-sec05-F36.must_match_memory_hook: Beginners are still learning driving skills

visual_sync.text_span: Beginners are still learning driving skills

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: Which four legal or financial consequences can follow driving after drinking?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Beyond courtroom fines and jail cells, high-risk insurance rates and revoked privileges follow impaired drivers for years.
sec05-card-sec05-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Heavy fines, steeper insurance, loss, jail

visual_sync.text_span: Heavy fines, steeper insurance, loss, jail

sec05-card-sec05-F38.question_text: Which three actions involving alcoholic beverages are prohibited for anyone under twenty-one?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.teaching_text: Even holding an unopened beverage container under twenty-one violates state law alongside buying or drinking.
sec05-card-sec05-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Under twenty-one cannot buy, possess, drink

visual_sync.text_span: Under twenty-one cannot buy, possess, drink

sec05-card-sec05-F39.question_text: Which three core driving tasks do alcohol and impairing drugs interfere with?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.teaching_text: Impairment hits the entire chain from spotting danger to reacting quickly and steering smoothly out of trouble.
sec05-card-sec05-F39.must_match_memory_hook: Perceiving surroundings, emergency response, skillful control

visual_sync.text_span: Perceiving surroundings, emergency response, skillful control

sec05-card-sec05-F40.teaching_text: Sitting behind the wheel to sleep it off still establishes physical control and triggers an impaired-driving arrest.
sec05-card-sec05-F40.must_match_memory_hook: Physical vehicle control suffices for arrest

sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Weakened color discrimination makes telling red brake lights or signals apart harder right as reflexes slow down.

visual_sync.text_span: Judgment, vision, color sense, reaction speed

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: What specific vision problems and misjudgments does the handbook link to alcohol?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Seeing double and focusing slowly wrecks your ability to judge distance, closing speed, and lane movement.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Because the very first drink dulls driving precision, the safest rule is skipping behind-the-wheel operation completely.

visual_sync.text_span: Impairment starts with drink number one

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: What responsibility does the handbook emphasize when a friend or relative has been drinking?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Stepping in to take keys or arrange a sober ride stops preventable tragedies before a loved one pulls out.
sec05-card-sec05-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Never let drinking friends drive away

sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Eight-hundredths is never a free pass if slurred reactions or unsafe weaving prove impairment at lower readings.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Even trace alcohol reaching two-hundredths of a percent triggers an underage impairment arrest in South Dakota.
sec05-card-sec05-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Under twenty-one arrested at zero two

visual_sync.text_span: Under twenty-one arrested at zero two

sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Chemical testing is not limited to roadside breath machines because blood and urine samples also measure concentration.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Once impaired driving is reasonably suspected, implied consent requires cooperating with the officer's lawful chemical test request.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.teaching_text: Practiced drinkers may walk or talk calmly while carrying a dangerously elevated bloodstream alcohol reading.

sec05-card-sec05-R24.question_text: Starting at what blood-alcohol concentration does crash risk climb even for drinkers who hide visible drunkenness?
sec05-card-sec05-R24.teaching_text: Masking outward slurring never shields brain timing once blood alcohol reaches five-hundredths of a percent or higher.

sec05-card-sec05-R25.question_text: What happens to a motorist's judgment and traffic decisions as blood-alcohol concentration continues to rise?
sec05-card-sec05-R25.teaching_text: Each upward tick in bloodstream alcohol further degrades judgment and accurate split-moment traffic choices.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.question_text: How is a repeat under-twenty-one zero-tolerance offense at zero point zero two percent classified and punished?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.teaching_text: A repeat underage zero-tolerance offense keeps Class two misdemeanor status while multiplying license loss sixfold to one-eighty days.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.must_match_memory_hook: Class one, year prison, thirty-day loss

sec05-card-sec05-R19.question_text: How does the DWI schedule classify and punish a second DWI offense?

sec05-card-sec05-R22.question_text: What mandatory jail sentence applies to unlicensed driving during a third-DWI license-loss period?

sec05-card-sec05-R26.question_text: When did South Dakota's THINK roadside program start, which two agencies teamed up, and what are its two goals?

sec05-card-sec05-R27.question_text: How many THINK posts and markers are placed along the state-highway right-of-way after a fatal crash?

sec05-card-sec05-R31.question_text: Which four side effects can stimulant or diet pills trigger behind the wheel?

sec05-card-sec05-R32.question_text: What two steps should you take before driving after taking an over-the-counter drug?

visual_sync.text_span: Antidepressants, painkillers, sleep aids, and sedatives

sec05-card-sec05-R35.question_text: When should you read prescription and packaging warnings, and whom should you ask when uncertain about driving side effects?
sec05-card-sec05-R35.teaching_text: Checking warnings before taking the dose—and consulting your doctor or pharmacist—prevents getting stranded away from home.
sec05-card-sec05-R35.must_match_memory_hook: Read before taking, ask medical pros

visual_sync.text_span: Read before taking, ask medical pros

sec05-card-sec05-R36.question_text: Which four driving abilities can illegal drugs impair in ways that resemble alcohol?
sec05-card-sec05-R36.teaching_text: Notice the handbook lists the exact same four impaired faculties—reflexes, judgment, sight, and alertness—for illegal drugs.
sec05-card-sec05-R36.must_match_memory_hook: Reflexes, judgment, sight, and alertness suffer

visual_sync.text_span: Reflexes, judgment, sight, and alertness suffer

sec05-card-sec05-R37.question_text: Which three driving problems or enforcement outcomes does the handbook report more often among marijuana users?
sec05-card-sec05-R37.teaching_text: Slower recovery from oncoming headlight glare pairs with higher error and traffic-arrest rates among marijuana users.
sec05-card-sec05-R37.must_match_memory_hook: More mistakes, glare trouble, violation arrests

visual_sync.text_span: More mistakes, glare trouble, violation arrests

sec05-card-sec05-R38.question_text: Why must you never combine drinking alcohol with taking other drugs before driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R38.teaching_text: One drink paired with medication can multiply impairment far beyond what either substance produces alone.
sec05-card-sec05-R38.must_match_memory_hook: Combos amplify alcohol or stack impairment

visual_sync.text_span: Combos amplify alcohol or stack impairment

sec05-card-sec05-R39.question_text: Which three mental processes can strong emotions disrupt while you are driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R39.teaching_text: Intense grief, excitement, or anger crowds out hazard processing just when traffic demands clear thinking.
sec05-card-sec05-R39.must_match_memory_hook: Strong emotions cloud thinking, attention, processing

visual_sync.text_span: Strong emotions cloud thinking, attention, processing

sec05-card-sec05-R40.question_text: What should an angry or overly excited motorist do before driving on?
