sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: What two signaling methods are recognized for communicating turns and lane changes?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Knowing left-arm hand signals keeps your intentions clear if a bulb burns out or sunlight washes lenses.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: Why must side and rear checks stay brief with your eyes snapping right back ahead?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Staring over your shoulder for two long seconds lets brake lights ahead turn into a rear-end crash.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: How should you handle blind-spot verification if one quick glance is not enough before changing lanes?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Breaking a complex merge into quick snapshots preserves forward awareness instead of driving blind down your lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: Which smaller road users require extra visual attention when pulling out from a curb or driveway?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Narrow silhouettes easily hide behind door pillars or parked SUVs right beside curb and driveway aprons.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: When is checking your mirror behind you most urgent while slowing down?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Braking abruptly for an unmarked driveway catches trailing drivers off guard when no traffic light warns them.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: How can smart parking selection cut down on risky reversing maneuvers?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Backing out of tight stalls accounts for countless lot fender-benders that forward pull-through parking avoids.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: What two visual checks must you perform before and during backing instead of trusting mirrors alone?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Low toys, pets, and toddlers below trunk height vanish completely inside rearview mirrors.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: At what pace should you reverse, and who should assist whenever available?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Walking-pace reverse speed plus a ground spotter standing clear gives instant stopping power if someone steps near.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: What rear hazard should you watch for in your mirrors on a long or steep downgrade?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Heavy rigs and buses gain momentum fast on steep grades and cannot shed speed quickly behind you.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: Which two calendar months does the handbook spotlight for heightened deer-collision alertness?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Autumn breeding and harvest movement push far more deer across highways during mid-to-late fall.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: At what two times of day are deer most active, and what visual clue betrays them along roadsides?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Spotting glowing pinpoints in ditch grass reveals deer poised to bolt well before their coats appear.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: What four actions should you take right away when headlight reflections show deer eyes beside the road?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Deer travel in herds, so one animal froze in ditch grass almost always has others trailing behind.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: Are deer crossings limited only to open country highways and rural backroads?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Wooded parks, river corridors, and suburban yards funnel deer straight across city streets year-round.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: What three elements work together to make up safe speed management?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Driving the posted number can still be unsafe or unlawful when traffic jams up or pavement turns slick.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: When should you shed speed for a curve so your tires track stably through the bend?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Shedding speed while wheels point straight keeps full tire grip available for cornering forces.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: What three situations call for dropping your curve entry speed even lower?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Entering a blind bend too hot leaves nowhere to stop if stalled cars or ice wait around the corner.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: What happens to tire grip if you slam the brakes after already entering a curve?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Demanding hard deceleration and sharp cornering at once overloads tire friction and triggers a slide.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: When precipitation or ice starts, why must you drop speed right away?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Fresh rain lifting road oil or thin ice cuts tire bite, stretching stops and spinning turns.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: What causes hydroplaning, and how do you help prevent it in wet weather?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Once steering tires plane atop pooled water, steering and braking vanish completely until tires touch asphalt.
sec14-card-sec14-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Slow down before water lifts tires

visual_sync.text_span: Slow down before water lifts tires

sec14-card-sec14-R12.question_text: What should you do when large pools of floodwater cover the road ahead?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.teaching_text: Floodwater hides washed-out pavement, stalls engines instantly, and sweeps vehicles off the roadway.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.question_text: From start to finish, what travel span does total stopping distance measure?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.teaching_text: Counting only brake marks ignores the yards your car covers while your brain spots danger and moves feet.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.question_text: How does raising your travel speed change what is needed to bring the vehicle to a stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.teaching_text: Kinetic energy climbs disproportionately with speed, multiplying every phase of stopping when emergencies strike.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.question_text: What does perception time measure, and how long does it average for an alert driver?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.teaching_text: Even wide-awake eyes need nearly a full second just to recognize brake lights or road hazards ahead.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.question_text: What action happens during reaction time, and what average duration does the handbook give?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.teaching_text: Pivoting your foot off the throttle onto the brake pedal burns almost another full second of forward roll.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.question_text: Roughly how far does braking distance alone run at fifty miles per hour on dry pavement with good brakes?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.teaching_text: Sliding more than half a football field after the pads clamp proves why tailgating at highway speeds fails.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.question_text: Why should you maintain an open space cushion around your vehicle in traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.teaching_text: Surrounding margins let you brake gently or steer out of trouble when nearby drivers make sudden mistakes.

sec14-card-sec14-R19.question_text: What minimum following interval in seconds should you keep under good conditions, and why?
sec14-card-sec14-R19.teaching_text: Anything tighter than four seconds blocks forward sightlines and erases reaction margin if traffic slams brakes.

sec14-card-sec14-R20.question_text: How do you use a roadside object to measure your following interval in seconds?
sec14-card-sec14-R20.teaching_text: Timing fixed shadows, signs, or overpass posts adjusts your physical gap automatically as speed rises.

sec14-card-sec14-R21.question_text: What should you do if your front bumper passes the landmark before you finish counting four seconds?
sec14-card-sec14-R21.teaching_text: Backing off throttle opens a true four-second buffer and verifying again confirms your gap stopped shrinking.

sec14-card-sec14-R22.question_text: How can you train your eyes to judge time distances more accurately down the road?
sec14-card-sec14-R22.teaching_text: Testing your visual guesses against real second counts sharpens your twenty-to-thirty-second scan accuracy.

sec14-card-sec14-R23.question_text: How must your following gap change when pavement turns wet, snowy, or icy?
sec14-card-sec14-R23.teaching_text: Four dry-road seconds will not stop you on ice or slush where tires need far more rollout room.

sec14-card-sec14-R24.question_text: How should you adjust speed when a trailing driver pulls out to pass you?
sec14-card-sec14-R24.teaching_text: Lifting slightly opens a merge pocket ahead of your hood and gets the passer out of oncoming lanes faster.

sec14-card-sec14-R25.question_text: Why must you open extra following distance behind motorcycles and bicycles, especially on slick or loose surfaces?
sec14-card-sec14-R25.teaching_text: Gravel, wet paint, ice, or metal bridge grates can spill a two-wheeler right in front of your tires.

sec14-card-sec14-R26.question_text: Behind which types of vehicles should you stay farther back because their drivers cannot easily see you?
sec14-card-sec14-R26.teaching_text: Operators of vans, buses, rigs, and trailers cannot spot a small car tucked directly behind their tailgates.

sec14-card-sec14-R27.question_text: How far back can a large truck's rear blind spot reach?
sec14-card-sec14-R27.teaching_text: Hanging inside that two-hundred-foot shadow hides you from the trucker's mirrors and blocks your view ahead.

sec14-card-sec14-R28.question_text: Why must you add extra following space when hauling heavy cargo or pulling a trailer?
sec14-card-sec14-R28.teaching_text: Loaded beds and trailers push forward hard under braking, demanding longer clear pavement to halt.

sec14-card-sec14-R29.question_text: Why should you widen your forward gap at night, in bad weather, or when someone tailgates you?
sec14-card-sec14-R29.teaching_text: Extra room ahead lets you brake gradually so a tailgater behind you does not slam your rear bumper.

sec14-card-sec14-R30.question_text: Why must you hold extra distance behind police cars, ambulances, and fire trucks?
sec14-card-sec14-R30.teaching_text: Responders may stop, turn across lanes, or swing wide without warning while managing active calls.

sec14-card-sec14-R31.question_text: Which three vehicle types require extra following room at railroad crossings because they must stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R31.teaching_text: School buses, transit buses, and hazmat tankers stop at tracks even when warning lights stay dark.

sec14-card-sec14-R32.question_text: Why should you leave extra room behind the car ahead when stopping on an uphill grade?
sec14-card-sec14-R32.teaching_text: Manual cars and heavy loads often drift backward a few feet as drivers move from brake to gas.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: What steering escape advantage does keeping a side-space cushion provide?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Having open pavement left or right lets you steer smoothly around sudden debris or drifting cars.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: Why should you avoid cruising right next to another vehicle in an adjacent lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Hovering beside another car hides you in its mirror blind zone while walling off your side escape path.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: Where should you position your car relative to the centerline on two-way roads when possible?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Hugging the yellow line leaves zero margin if an oncoming driver drifts wide around a bend.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: How can you help vehicles merging onto the roadway when traffic allows?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Moving over a lane or easing throttle prevents awkward ramp standoffs and last-second sideswipes.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: How should you position and time your pass around walkers and bicyclists, especially children?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Kids on bikes wobble without warning, so waiting for a full adjacent-lane pass prevents tragic contact.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: Where within your lane should you ease when a large truck or bus passes you?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: Edging slightly toward the outer stripe adds buffer against trailer sway and wind buffeting.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: How should you position yourself on a multilane road instead of riding beside another car?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Staggering your position into open pockets keeps every adjacent lane drift away from your doors.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: Why must you hold extra clearance when driving past a line of parked cars?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Unseen drivers fling doors open and pedestrians step between bumpers without glancing back.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: How should you position your car when squeezed between hazards on both sides at once?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Shifting extra inches away from a vulnerable cyclist or oncoming truck cuts the deadlier crash risk.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: How should you handle meeting an oncoming car and a bicyclist at the exact same spot?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Waiting two seconds for opposing traffic to pass opens plenty of room to clear the cyclist safely.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: What two habits of yours make it easier for a driver behind you to keep a safe distance?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Consistent speed and advance warnings stop trailing drivers from creeping close or braking late.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: Where should you pull over to load or unload passengers whenever possible?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Stopping inside active lanes exposes stepping passengers and trailing cars to sudden collisions.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: What should you do before backing into a parallel space when traffic approaches behind you?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Letting close followers clear first prevents someone from nosing right into the stall you are backing toward.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: Which lane belongs to slower traffic on multilane roads, and what if you delay cars behind you?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Camping slowly in left lanes triggers risky right-side passing and road frustration behind you.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: How should you shed a tailgater on multilane versus two-lane roads?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Giving a tailgater an easy legal pass puts aggressive risk well ahead of your windshield instead of behind.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: Why must you never tap or slam the brakes abruptly to warn off a tailgater?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Sudden braking when someone is feet off your bumper practically guarantees a rear-end crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: Why must you leave generous room when pulling in front of or maneuvering near trucks and buses?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Cutting tightly ahead of a loaded semi steals the long braking buffer its heavy weight demands.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: Where and how many vehicles at a time should you generally overtake?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Stringing multiple cars into one pass multiplies your time in the oncoming lane if gaps shrink.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: How quickly should you finish an overtake and get out of the passing lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Dawdling in the opposing lane stretches your head-on exposure every extra second.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: About how many seconds does a fifty-five mile per hour pass take in the handbook example?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Ten full seconds in the opposing lane demands far more clear road than most beginners guess.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, how much total clear distance do two closing vehicles cover during a ten-second pass?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Both cars eat up over eight hundred feet apiece, closing a third-mile gap shockingly fast.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: Why must you hold back from passing whenever an oncoming vehicle's closing gap feels uncertain?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Straight-on headlights barely grow until the final seconds, fooling drivers into deadly misjudgments.
sec15-card-sec15-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Distant cars close faster than seen

visual_sync.text_span: Distant cars close faster than seen

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: How much clear sightline is advised for passing, and where near hills or curves must you stay back?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: An unseen car cresting a rise inside a third of a mile leaves nowhere to abort a pass.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: Which three cross-traffic locations are off-limits for passing?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: Drivers pulling out of side streets or shopping lots rarely expect an overtaker charging up the wrong lane.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: How can the vehicle you are overtaking hide cross-traffic or train hazards from your view?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Using a tall van or truck as a blind screen hides trains and left-turning cars until impact.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: How does the handbook contrast car length with multi-trailer trucks to show why truck passes take longer?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Clearing seventy-five-plus feet of trailers takes much more open pavement than zipping past a compact sedan.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: What roadside or surface hazards ahead could force the car you are passing to swerve into you?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: A driver dodging a pothole or cyclist ahead will swerve left straight into your passing lane.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.question_text: What lane-return requirement must exist before starting a pass?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.teaching_text: Assuming tightly packed drivers will brake to let you squeeze back in gambles your life head-on.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.question_text: Is passing permitted when approaching a railroad grade crossing?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.teaching_text: Passing near tracks risks meeting an unseen train while trapped beside traffic stopped for the crossing.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.question_text: What visual cue in your inside rearview mirror confirms safe separation to move back right after passing?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.teaching_text: Seeing the passed car's entire front grille in your center mirror proves you will not clip its fender.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.question_text: Which drivers and pedestrians need extra space because they may not see your vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.teaching_text: Anyone backing blind, peering around cargo, or navigating with a white cane or guide dog relies on you.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.question_text: Which four groups of distracted people along the roadway deserve extra space and caution?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.teaching_text: Workers hustling packages or cones and children chasing toys focus on their task instead of traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.question_text: What four clues point to confused drivers or pedestrians who may make sudden unpredictable moves?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.teaching_text: Lost tourists reading street signs and alcohol-impaired walkers brake or step into lanes without warning.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.question_text: Why must you hold clear of large trucks, buses, and wide loads, especially inside roundabouts?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.teaching_text: Long trailers track across multiple lanes in tight circles and wide loads overhang lane stripes.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.question_text: What should you do if another driver botches a pass or lunges into a sudden lane change?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.teaching_text: Yielding a few car lengths saves everyone from a multi-car wreck when somebody miscalculates.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.question_text: How do you separate multiple road hazards before reaching them at the same instant?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.teaching_text: Easing off early lets oncoming traffic clear before you reach a narrow bridge, parked car, or walker.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.question_text: Which side gets the bigger space cushion when two hazards cannot be separated in time?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.teaching_text: Brushing a parked fender bends metal, whereas crowding a child on a bicycle risks a life.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.question_text: Why should you switch on headlights in rain, snow, or fog even during daytime?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.teaching_text: Gray spray and swirling snow camouflage unlit cars long before darkness falls.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.question_text: What two everyday triggers does the handbook recommend for turning your headlights on?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.teaching_text: Linking headlights directly to windshield wipers and dusk stops your car from disappearing in gloom.

sec15-card-sec15-F40.question_text: Why are parking lamps unacceptable as a substitute for headlights while driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F40.teaching_text: Dim amber marker bulbs neither light the pavement nor warn oncoming traffic that your car is moving.

sec15-card-sec15-F41.question_text: Why should you turn headlights on when driving away from a low rising or setting sun?
sec15-card-sec15-F41.teaching_text: Drivers staring straight into sunrise or sunset glare lose silhouettes unless your headlights pierce through.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: How much farther do high beams reach at night compared with low beams when no oncoming car is near?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Doubling your lit sightline on dark rural highways prevents outrunning your headlights at cruising speed.
sec15-card-sec15-R01.must_match_memory_hook: High beams reach twice as far

visual_sync.text_span: High beams reach twice as far

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must you dim your high beams?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Blinding an approaching driver five hundred feet out risks steering them straight across the centerline.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: Within what following distance, or in what traffic density, must you stay on low beams?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: High beams reflected off side and center mirrors dazzle the driver ahead just like oncoming glare.
sec15-card-sec15-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Under five hundred feet, heavy traffic

visual_sync.text_span: Under five hundred feet, heavy traffic

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: Which headlight beam and auxiliary lights belong in fog, falling snow, or heavy rain?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: High beams bounce straight off water droplets and snowflakes into a blinding white wall.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: Is it ever proper to drive with only your parking lamps switched on?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Cruising on marker lights tricks cross-traffic into thinking your car is sitting still at the curb.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: What two steps should you take if an oncoming driver forgets to dim glaring high beams?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Retaliating with steady brights blinds both drivers, whereas tracking the right fog line guides you safely past.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: When are daytime running lamps no substitute for switching on full headlights?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Daytime running lamps often leave taillights completely dark and project too little beam for night or storms.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: What reminder comes with manually running full headlights during the day on cars without daytime lamps?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Manual headlamps add daytime visibility nicely, provided you shut them off so the battery stays charged.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: What is the horn's core purpose, and how should you sound it when danger is not immediate?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: A gentle tap alerts nearby road users without startling them into erratic steering or panic stops.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: When can a light horn tap warn a walker or cyclist, versus when must you yield quietly instead?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Pedestrians crossing intersections hold right-of-way, so honking to push them aside violates yielding rules.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: Which driver mistakes justify a quick, light warning tap on the horn?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: Catching a distracted or blind-spotted driver with a quick beep stops a lane-drift sideswipe early.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.question_text: At what three sight-restricted terrain or city spots can a light horn tap prevent a surprise collision?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.teaching_text: Sound travels past brick walls and hill crests where windshields cannot yet see emerging noses.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.question_text: Which two urgent emergencies call for a sharp, loud blast on the horn?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.teaching_text: When impact is seconds away or brakes fail, an unmistakable blast commands immediate evasive action.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.question_text: What three everyday social or emotional uses of the horn does the handbook forbid?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.teaching_text: Angry or friendly honks confuse nearby traffic and distract drivers scanning for genuine crash warnings.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.question_text: Around which three road users or animals must you keep off the horn completely?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.teaching_text: Horn blasts disorient pedestrians listening for traffic cues and spook horses or cattle into bolting.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.question_text: How should you warn approaching traffic behind a broken-down vehicle and get assistance?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.teaching_text: Retroreflective triangles or flares set well back give fast-closing drivers warning long before taillights.

sec15-card-sec15-R17.question_text: Where should you steer a troubled vehicle first, and which lights go on right away?
sec15-card-sec15-R17.teaching_text: Coasting onto the shoulder while rolling saves you from being stranded inside a live high-speed lane.

sec15-card-sec15-R18.question_text: If your disabled car cannot clear the pavement completely, what terrain spots must you avoid stopping past?
sec15-card-sec15-R18.teaching_text: Parking just beyond a blind hill crest or tight bend gives oncoming traffic zero room to stop.

sec15-card-sec15-R19.question_text: Where should occupants wait during a breakdown, and what tire repair mistake must you never make?
sec15-card-sec15-R19.teaching_text: Crouching beside a lug wrench inside a live traffic lane puts your body inches from distracted bumpers.

sec15-card-sec15-R20.question_text: Besides hazard flashers, what visual distress cues tell passing patrols your parked vehicle needs help?
sec15-card-sec15-R20.teaching_text: Universal breakdown markers draw highway assistance without requiring you to wave beside fast traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-R21.question_text: How should you handle driving near or overtaking through another vehicle's side-and-rear blind area?
sec15-card-sec15-R21.teaching_text: Moving decisively past quarter-panel blind spots keeps lane-changing drivers from forgetting you are there.

sec15-card-sec15-R22.question_text: Which two positions around a large truck or bus must you never linger in?
sec15-card-sec15-R22.teaching_text: Trailer blowouts, wide turns, and huge blind spots punish cars camping beside or under a rig.

sec15-card-sec15-R23.question_text: How far ahead of the cab and behind the trailer do a large truck's blind zones reach?
sec15-card-sec15-R23.teaching_text: High hoods hide compact cars twenty feet forward while trailers block two hundred feet astern.
sec15-card-sec15-R23.must_match_memory_hook: Twenty feet front, two hundred back

visual_sync.text_span: Twenty feet front, two hundred back

sec15-card-sec15-R24.question_text: What mirror check tells you whether a truck or bus driver can actually see your vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-R24.teaching_text: Line-of-sight works both ways in glass, so an empty side mirror means you sit completely hidden.

sec15-card-sec15-R25.question_text: Why must you warn surrounding drivers before slowing down or changing direction?
sec15-card-sec15-R25.teaching_text: Other drivers cannot read your mind, so blinkers and brake taps prevent split-second surprises.

sec15-card-sec15-R26.question_text: Which maneuvers require turn signals, including both halves of passing, even when the road looks empty?
sec15-card-sec15-R26.teaching_text: The motorcycle or pedestrian you failed to spot is the exact person your automatic signal saves.

sec15-card-sec15-R27.question_text: Why must you avoid signaling a hundred feet early if another driveway or street sits before your turn?
sec15-card-sec15-R27.teaching_text: A driver poised at an intervening driveway may pull straight across your bow thinking you are turning there.

sec15-card-sec15-R28.question_text: When should you flip your blinker on if a car waits at an entrance just short of your turn?
sec15-card-sec15-R28.teaching_text: Waiting until your nose clears the waiting car removes any doubt about which corner you want.

sec15-card-sec15-R29.question_text: What dashboard check belongs right after completing a gentle turn or lane change?
sec15-card-sec15-R29.teaching_text: Gentle steering angles often fail to self-cancel the stalk, broadcasting false turns down the block.

sec15-card-sec15-R30.question_text: How should you alert trailing drivers before making an unexpected slowdown or stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R30.teaching_text: Flashing your brake lamps three or four quick times grabs peripheral attention much faster than steady glow.

sec15-card-sec15-R31.question_text: Which three road situations call for extra advance slowdown warnings to traffic behind you?
sec15-card-sec15-R31.teaching_text: Trailing drivers expect steady speed until an intersection unless you warn them about midblock stops or jams.

sec15-card-sec15-R32.question_text: When are hand-and-arm turn signals useful even today, including which vintage vehicle cutoff date?
sec15-card-sec15-R32.teaching_text: Glaring sun washes out dim tail lenses, and pre-July nineteen fifty-eight classics may lack electric blinkers.

sec15-card-sec15-R33.question_text: How do you position your left arm and hand to signal a left turn?
sec15-card-sec15-R33.teaching_text: Pointing horizontally out the driver window gives an unmistakable directional arrow to trailing traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-R34.question_text: How do you hold your left arm and hand to signal a right turn?
sec15-card-sec15-R34.teaching_text: Bending your elbow ninety degrees skyward rises clearly above the roofline for cars behind you.

sec15-card-sec15-R35.question_text: How do you position your left arm and hand to signal slowing down or stopping?
sec15-card-sec15-R35.teaching_text: Dropping your open hand toward the pavement warns following traffic to check speed right away.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.question_text: What three vehicle controls give you ways to avoid a crash or soften its impact?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.teaching_text: Fixating only on the brake pedal overlooks open lanes where quick steering or throttle escapes impact.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.question_text: What two advantages do anti-lock brakes provide during a hard stop?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.teaching_text: Preventing wheel lockup lets your front tires keep turning the car around the obstacle ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.question_text: How should you work the brake pedal during an emergency stop with anti-lock brakes?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.teaching_text: Pumping an anti-lock pedal defeats its rapid computer pulsing and stretches out your stopping distance.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.question_text: What sensations or sounds from an anti-lock brake pedal are completely normal in a hard stop?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.teaching_text: Startled drivers sometimes lift off a buzzing pedal when that chatter proves the anti-lock valves are working.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.question_text: Can you steer during anti-lock braking, and where should drivers without anti-lock brakes check technique?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.teaching_text: Knowing ahead of time whether your car uses anti-lock or conventional brakes prevents panic errors.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.question_text: How should your hands and eyes work when steering rapidly around a sudden road hazard?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.teaching_text: Looking directly at your open escape lane guides your hands past both the obstacle and adjacent cars.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.question_text: What steering recovery comes right after clearing a hazard and before you slow down?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.teaching_text: Hitting the brakes while the chassis is still yawing sideways snaps the rear tires into a spin.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.question_text: In what incoming-crash scenario can pressing the accelerator prevent an impact?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.teaching_text: Surging ahead a car length can clear an intersection or bumper when another vehicle charges in.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.question_text: What three driving or traction factors commonly set off a vehicle skid?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.teaching_text: Asking tires for more speed or sharper braking than road grip supports breaks traction loose.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.question_text: What should your foot and eyes do the instant your vehicle begins to skid?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.teaching_text: Freeing rolling tires restores grip while fixing your gaze down the lane guides smooth recovery steering.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.question_text: How should you recover if your tires drop off the pavement edge onto the shoulder?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel hard against a pavement lip at highway speed slingshots cars across oncoming lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.question_text: What routine habit lowers your odds of facing a sudden mechanical emergency on the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.teaching_text: Worn belts, old brake fluid, and neglected tires give warning in the shop long before snapping.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.question_text: How must you treat an illuminated brake warning light on the dashboard?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.teaching_text: A lit brake lamp signals hydraulic trouble or low fluid that can rob stopping power suddenly.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.question_text: How should you use the parking brake if your main service brakes fail while rolling?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.teaching_text: Ratcheting or pressing gently slows the rear drums without locking them into an uncontrollable spin.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.question_text: What is the handbook's next step if gradual parking-brake pressure still fails to stop you?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.teaching_text: Cutting engine power removes forward drive while you guide the coasting car onto a safe shoulder.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.question_text: May you limp a vehicle down the road once you discover its brakes do not work?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.teaching_text: Even low-speed neighborhood creeping without working brakes turns the first hill or child into disaster.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.question_text: How does a front tire blowout feel at the wheel compared with a rear tire blowout?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.teaching_text: Recognizing whether the nose yanks or the tail shakes keeps you from overcorrecting in surprise.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.question_text: What should your hands and right foot do immediately when a tire blows out?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.teaching_text: Holding steady down your lane while lifting smoothly off the gas keeps weight balanced across remaining tires.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.question_text: Why should you stay off the brake pedal right after a blowout and let momentum bleed naturally?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.teaching_text: Clamping the brakes on a shredded tire digs the rim into asphalt and spins the car sideways.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.question_text: Where should you stop after bringing a blown tire under control, and what comes next?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.teaching_text: Rolling fully off live pavement with hazard lights flashing protects you before any jack comes out.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.question_text: What happens to the steering if the engine stalls while moving, and how should you grip?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.teaching_text: Power assist drops out when the engine dies, requiring firm two-handed muscle to turn the wheels.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.question_text: How should you brake and position the car after the engine quits in traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.teaching_text: Vacuum brake assist holds only one or two boosted presses, so one steady push beats repeated pumping.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.question_text: What steps follow once you coast a stalled vehicle safely off the roadway?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.teaching_text: Testing one restart off-road checks for a fluke stall before raising distress signals for roadside help.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.question_text: How does the handbook's stuck-accelerator emergency sequence begin?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.teaching_text: Disconnecting runaway engine power into Neutral stops the car from accelerating further down traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.question_text: How do you finish stopping a stuck-accelerator vehicle, and what must happen before driving again?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.teaching_text: Driving again before a mechanic fixes a binding throttle cable invites a repeat runaway at speed.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.question_text: What two priorities apply whenever your vehicle breaks down along a highway?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.teaching_text: High-speed traffic needs early visual warning while dispatchers send patrol protection or a tow.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.question_text: Where should a disabled vehicle go immediately, and which warning lights belong on?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.teaching_text: Getting clear of travel stripes and flipping hazard lamps cuts secondary rear-end crash odds sharply.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.question_text: About how many feet behind a disabled vehicle does the handbook place warning flares?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.teaching_text: Setting flares a few hundred feet upstream gives highway drivers braking room before reaching your bumper.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.question_text: What should you try first if your headlights go dark at night, and what backup lights help you exit?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.teaching_text: Working the dimmer or main switch may clear a dirty contact, and hazard or fog lamps guide you off-road.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.question_text: What should an uninvolved driver do when emergency crews are already working a crash scene?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.teaching_text: Pulling over when paramedics are already on scene clogs shoulders while responders walk near live lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.question_text: Why must drivers never drive toward a crash, fire, or disaster area just to watch?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.teaching_text: Curious rubberneckers choke access roads that fire engines and ambulances need open to save lives.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.question_text: What must every crash-involved driver do immediately, including after bumping a parked car?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.teaching_text: Driving off from even a parking-lot scrape turns a minor claim into an unlawful hit-and-run.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.question_text: When someone is hurt or killed in a crash, whom must you call and how long must you stay?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.teaching_text: Leaving an injury crash before officers gather required statements violates mandatory crash-reporting duties.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.question_text: What three supply types does the handbook recommend carrying in an onboard emergency kit?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.teaching_text: Stowing flares, bandages, and hand tools in your trunk prepares you before trouble strikes.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.question_text: Where should you stop after a crash, and what should you do if your vehicle still drives safely?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.teaching_text: Leaving drivable cars parked mid-intersection invites a far worse high-speed secondary pileup.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.question_text: Where must you never stand or walk while dealing with a roadside crash?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.teaching_text: Approaching motorists staring at crumpled metal often miss people standing on live asphalt.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.question_text: What two fire-prevention steps belong around wrecked vehicles at a crash scene?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.teaching_text: Ruptured fuel lines leak vapor invisible in daylight that one hot spark or cigarette can ignite.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.question_text: How should you treat fallen power lines lying on or beside the roadway?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.teaching_text: Silent, unsparking utility cables can still carry lethal high voltage across wet pavement.

sec16-card-sec16-R16.question_text: How do you keep oncoming motorists from plowing into an active crash site?
sec16-card-sec16-R16.teaching_text: Setting warning markers upstream alerts fast traffic before curves or darkness hide the wreck.

sec16-card-sec16-R17.question_text: Whom should you summon when crash injuries occur, and what hazard must you mention on the call?
sec16-card-sec16-R17.teaching_text: Dispatchers roll fire suppression rigs alongside ambulances immediately when callers report smoke or flames.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.question_text: What single piece of safety gear is the handbook's primary defense when a crash is unavoidable?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.teaching_text: Three-point belts hold occupants inside the survival space through initial and secondary impacts alike.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.question_text: How should your body, head, and foot prepare right before your car is struck from behind?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.teaching_text: Eliminating neck gap against the headrest reduces whiplash while braking stops forward lunges into cross traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.question_text: How do seat belts help the driver survive and recover during a side-impact collision?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.teaching_text: Staying anchored behind the wheel lets you brake or steer away from trees and oncoming cars afterward.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.question_text: Do standard front dashboard airbags protect occupants against side-impact forces in the handbook's discussion?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.teaching_text: Dashboard bags trigger for frontal deceleration, leaving belts to restrain sideways occupant motion.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.question_text: If a frontal crash cannot be avoided, how should you steer to reduce impact severity?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.teaching_text: Deflecting at an angle spreads crash energy over time instead of taking full head-on force.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.question_text: Why must you keep belts fastened and stay ready to control the car during a frontal airbag crash?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.teaching_text: Front bags vent immediately after inflating, so belts and alert hands stop follow-up collisions.

sec16-card-sec16-R18.question_text: Under what two extreme dangers only should you move an injured crash victim?
sec16-card-sec16-R18.teaching_text: Shifting someone with a hidden spinal fracture risks permanent paralysis unless flames or traffic threaten.

sec16-card-sec16-R19.question_text: Which crash victims get checked first, and which vital sign comes before bleeding?
sec16-card-sec16-R19.teaching_text: Quiet, motionless occupants face the gravest airway danger, making breathing the top triage check.
sec16-card-sec16-R19.must_match_memory_hook: Silent victims first, breathing before blood

visual_sync.text_span: Silent victims first, breathing before blood

sec16-card-sec16-R20.question_text: What straightforward first-aid action does the handbook advise to control bleeding?
sec16-card-sec16-R20.teaching_text: Steady direct pressure over a clean pad slows blood loss effectively until paramedics arrive.

sec16-card-sec16-R21.question_text: What may you give an injured crash victim to drink while waiting for paramedics?
sec16-card-sec16-R21.teaching_text: Even plain water can cause choking or complicate emergency anesthesia and internal-injury surgery.

sec16-card-sec16-R22.question_text: How should you help prevent shock in an injured person at a crash scene?
sec16-card-sec16-R22.teaching_text: Conserving body heat with a jacket or blanket stabilizes circulation after crash trauma.

sec16-card-sec16-R23.question_text: Whose names and addresses should you gather after a collision?
sec16-card-sec16-R23.teaching_text: Bystanders drive away quickly, so recording witness contacts early preserves neutral crash accounts.

sec16-card-sec16-R24.question_text: What five categories of driver, vehicle, and coverage details should drivers exchange at a crash?
sec16-card-sec16-R24.teaching_text: Swapping complete license, tag, vehicle, and policy details keeps claims and police reports accurate.

sec16-card-sec16-R25.question_text: What physical details should you document on scene, and whom must you share crash info with on request?
sec16-card-sec16-R25.teaching_text: Recording exact dent locations and cooperating with responding officers prevents disputed damage claims later.

sec16-card-sec16-R26.question_text: What must you do if you cannot locate the owner after striking a parked vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-R26.teaching_text: Tucking clear contact info with the crash date and hour fulfills your duty when owners are away.

sec16-card-sec16-R27.question_text: In what order do you notify police and your insurance company after an injury or fatal crash?
sec16-card-sec16-R27.teaching_text: Immediate scene reporting triggers official investigation first, followed promptly by insurance notice.

sec16-card-sec16-R28.question_text: Who can submit a required crash report if injuries keep the driver from filing it?
sec16-card-sec16-R28.teaching_text: Allowing a passenger, relative, or owner to file ensures hospitalization never causes a reporting violation.

sec16-card-sec16-R29.question_text: What two steps apply if you damage unattended property and cannot find its owner?
sec16-card-sec16-R29.teaching_text: Reporting broken signs, fences, or mailboxes to law enforcement plus leaving a note prevents hit-and-run charges.

sec16-card-sec16-R30.question_text: Which five specific items must appear on the note left at damaged unattended property?
sec16-card-sec16-R30.teaching_text: Including license and tag numbers alongside contact info, timestamp, and damage satisfies full legal disclosure.

sec16-card-sec16-R31.question_text: What does the unattended-property guidance advise regarding police arrival and leaving a crash scene?
sec16-card-sec16-R31.teaching_text: Staying put until an officer arrives protects you from criminal leaving-the-scene penalties.

sec16-card-sec16-R32.question_text: Which three violations sit first, second, and third in the handbook's injury-and-fatal-crash table?
sec16-card-sec16-R32.teaching_text: Everyday inattention and following too closely actually outrank impaired driving in total serious wrecks.

sec16-card-sec16-R33.question_text: Which three violations occupy fourth, fifth, and sixth place in the serious-crash ranking?
sec16-card-sec16-R33.teaching_text: Intersection shortcuts like rolling stops, sloppy turns, and ignoring signals fill the middle crash ranks.

sec16-card-sec16-R34.question_text: Which violations round out positions seven through ten in the handbook's crash-violation table?
sec16-card-sec16-R34.teaching_text: Outrunning weather, reckless moves, blind alley pullouts, and unfiled wrecks complete the top-ten list.

sec17-card-sec17-F01.question_text: What two habits reduce crash risk when sharing the road with everyone else?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.teaching_text: Courtesy and predictable signals eliminate guessing games between drivers, riders, and walkers.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.question_text: Must you yield to pedestrians only inside painted crosswalk stripes?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.teaching_text: Every street corner carries a legal crossing whether white paint is faded or absent.

sec17-card-sec17-F03.question_text: What must you do whenever a pedestrian crosses with a white cane or guide dog?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.teaching_text: Rolling slowly near a blind pedestrian masks traffic sound cues and risks direct contact.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.question_text: Who goes first if a pedestrian is still crossing the intersection when your signal turns green?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.teaching_text: A fresh green bulb gives permission to proceed only after people already in the crosswalk clear.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.question_text: What pedestrian responsibility remains whenever you make a legal turn on red?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.teaching_text: Drivers craning left for a traffic gap often roll forward straight into someone stepping off the right curb.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.question_text: How must you handle approaching a parked or stopped vehicle that could hide a crossing walker?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.teaching_text: Overtaking a stopped car in the next lane is a classic setup for hitting a hidden pedestrian.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.question_text: Where is scanning for pedestrians before reversing especially vital?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.teaching_text: Shoppers pushing carts and distracted kids weave constantly behind bumpers in crowded lots.
sec17-card-sec17-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Scan busy parking lots before backing

visual_sync.text_span: Scan busy parking lots before backing

sec17-card-sec17-F08.question_text: What hazard should you anticipate along residential streets and playgrounds?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.teaching_text: Small children sit below hood height until the split second they sprint after a ball.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.question_text: When do reduced school-zone speeds apply, and how must you respond to crossing patrols?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.teaching_text: Flashing beacons, children near the curb, and crossing-guard paddles each carry binding legal authority.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.question_text: How does South Dakota traffic guidance classify a bicycle riding on the roadway?
sec17-card-sec17-F10.teaching_text: Treating cyclists as lawful vehicle operators clarifies lane rights and intersection priority.

sec17-card-sec17-F11.question_text: Why must drivers stay extra alert around bicyclists of varying experience?
sec17-card-sec17-F11.teaching_text: Inexperienced cyclists may dodge potholes suddenly, blow stop signs, or ride dark after sunset.

sec17-card-sec17-F12.question_text: At which two crossing points must motorists yield to bicyclists?
sec17-card-sec17-F12.teaching_text: Multi-use trails and painted bike lanes carry fast-rolling riders straight across street aprons.

sec17-card-sec17-F13.question_text: Apart from driveway access, emergencies, official work, or police orders, what is forbidden in a bike lane?
sec17-card-sec17-F13.teaching_text: Blocking a painted bike lane forces riders to swerve abruptly into faster motor traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.question_text: How should you time a turn when a bicyclist is riding through the intersection?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.teaching_text: Racing ahead to beat a rider to the corner causes classic right-hook and left-cross impacts.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.question_text: Why must you never pull ahead of a bicyclist and brake hard?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.teaching_text: Four wide car tires shed speed far faster than skinny bicycle rims, slamming a trailing rider into your trunk.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.question_text: Why should you avoid honking right beside or behind a cyclist unless preventing a crash?
sec17-card-sec17-F16.teaching_text: A sudden blast feet behind an open rider can jolt handlebars straight into your bumper.

sec17-card-sec17-F17.question_text: Which riders are especially prone to rolling off a sidewalk directly into your travel lane?
sec17-card-sec17-F17.teaching_text: Young riders jump curbs and driveway ramps without glancing back for approaching traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-F18.question_text: What turning mistake across a bicyclist's travel line must drivers never commit?
sec17-card-sec17-F18.teaching_text: Whipping right across a straight-moving bike leaves the rider nowhere to go except your passenger door.

sec17-card-sec17-F19.question_text: Even though cyclists must ride with traffic, where should your eyes still look for them?
sec17-card-sec17-F19.teaching_text: Not every rider follows the rulebook, so checking both directions catches wrong-way cyclists before turns.

sec17-card-sec17-F20.question_text: Why do wet, sandy, or gravel-strewn roads demand extra space around bicyclists?
sec17-card-sec17-F20.teaching_text: Thin two-wheel contact patches wash out instantly on grit or puddles that four-wheel cars barely feel.

sec17-card-sec17-F21.question_text: Besides hand signals, what rider movement warns that a cyclist plans to turn or shift lanes?
sec17-card-sec17-F21.teaching_text: Rough bumps or braking often keep both hands clamped on the bars, making shoulder checks your best clue.

sec17-card-sec17-F22.question_text: What check is mandatory before swinging open the street-side door of a parked car?
sec17-card-sec17-F22.teaching_text: Flung-open car doors drop cyclists onto live asphalt before they have a fraction of a second to swerve.

sec17-card-sec17-F23.question_text: Where is checking for approaching bicycles before backing out especially critical?
sec17-card-sec17-F23.teaching_text: Neighborhood driveways and school blocks carry steady streams of fast, quiet student riders.

sec17-card-sec17-F24.question_text: How much side clearance must you give a bicycle when passing where the limit is thirty-five miles per hour or lower?
sec17-card-sec17-F24.teaching_text: Three full feet measured from your widest right mirror or cargo edge protects riders from mirror strikes.

sec17-card-sec17-F25.question_text: What minimum passing clearance applies around a bicycle when the posted speed limit exceeds thirty-five miles per hour?
sec17-card-sec17-F25.teaching_text: Higher highway speeds create wind blast that demands doubling your buffer to six full feet.

sec17-card-sec17-F26.question_text: May you straddle a centerline or lane stripe to pass a bicycle safely, and how long must separation hold?
sec17-card-sec17-F26.teaching_text: Pulling back right too early clips the front wheel, so hold full three-or-six-foot spacing until clear.

sec17-card-sec17-F27.question_text: What misdemeanor level does South Dakota statute assign to violating the bicycle-passing clearance law?
sec17-card-sec17-F27.teaching_text: State law backs the three-foot and six-foot bicycle buffers with criminal misdemeanor teeth.

sec17-card-sec17-F28.question_text: How much lane width belongs to a motorcycle compared with a passenger car?
sec17-card-sec17-F28.teaching_text: Squeezing into the same lane beside a rider steals the side-to-side room needed to dodge road hazards.

sec17-card-sec17-F29.question_text: Where must you look carefully for narrow motorcycles, especially right before turning left?
sec17-card-sec17-F29.teaching_text: Left-turning cars misjudging a slim oncoming headlight cause the deadliest multi-vehicle motorcycle crashes.

sec17-card-sec17-F30.question_text: Why must you wait before pulling out in front of a motorcycle with a flashing turn signal?
sec17-card-sec17-F30.teaching_text: Many motorcycle switches do not self-cancel, so trusting a blinking bulb without rider slowdown causes crashes.

sec17-card-sec17-F31.question_text: How many seconds behind a motorcycle should you stay on dry pavement, and what about rain?
sec17-card-sec17-F31.teaching_text: Motorcycles shed speed briskly by downshifting without even lighting a brake lamp, demanding four-plus seconds.

sec17-card-sec17-F32.question_text: Which six road-surface hazards routinely prompt a motorcyclist to shift position inside the lane?
sec17-card-sec17-F32.teaching_text: Grooved asphalt, tar seams, rails, and gravel force riders across their lane to stay upright.

sec17-card-sec17-F33.question_text: How does the typical travel speed of scooters and mopeds compare with full-size motorcycles?
sec17-card-sec17-F33.teaching_text: Recognizing smaller wheels and engines early keeps you from closing way too fast from behind.

sec17-card-sec17-F34.question_text: More than how many crashes occur each year between passenger cars and commercial vehicles?
sec17-card-sec17-F34.teaching_text: Hundreds of thousands of yearly car-truck collisions highlight how unforgiving heavy-rig physics are.

sec17-card-sec17-F35.question_text: In what four operational ways do commercial rigs need more margin than passenger cars?
sec17-card-sec17-F35.teaching_text: Massive weight and trailer length slow acceleration, widen turns, hide cars, and stretch braking.

sec17-card-sec17-F36.question_text: In the commercial-vehicle overview, what minimum dry-road stopping distance is given for a loaded truck at fifty-five miles per hour?
sec17-card-sec17-F36.teaching_text: Needing nearly a full football field on dry pavement shows why cutting off a semi fails.

sec17-card-sec17-F37.question_text: At least how many feet can a large bus require to come to a stop?
sec17-card-sec17-F37.teaching_text: Heavy passenger coaches carry tremendous momentum that stretches emergency stops past three hundred feet.

sec17-card-sec17-F38.question_text: Besides mirror blind spots, what other danger zones around a truck or bus count as No-Zones?
sec17-card-sec17-F38.teaching_text: Even where a trucker sees you ahead, squeezing in too tight steals safe braking and steering room.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.question_text: Around which sides of a large truck or bus do blind areas exist?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.teaching_text: Drivers remember trailer sides and backs but often forget the tall blind pocket ahead of the grille.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.question_text: Where does a large truck's right-side blind area start, and how far back can it stretch?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.teaching_text: Passing slowly on a semi's right hides your entire car down the longest blind zone on the rig.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.question_text: What must you assume whenever you cannot see a commercial driver's face in the rig's side mirror?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.teaching_text: Mirrors reflect along a two-way path, so losing eye contact means your car vanished from view.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.question_text: Why should you stay alongside a large truck or bus only long enough to complete a pass?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.teaching_text: Wind gusts, road debris, or sudden lane shifts leave zero room for a car cruising beside trailer wheels.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.question_text: In the No-Zone stopping comparison, at least how many feet does a loaded truck take from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.teaching_text: Ideal tires and adjusted brakes still leave a loaded rig rolling more than a football field.

sec17-card-sec17-R06.question_text: How does that loaded-truck stopping distance compare with a passenger car's stopping distance?
sec17-card-sec17-R06.teaching_text: Fifty-plus percent extra rollout explains why trucks rear-end cars that dart in and hit the brakes.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.question_text: What mirror check and speed habit apply before and after merging back ahead of a passed truck?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.teaching_text: Waiting for the entire grille in your mirror and keeping pace protects the trucker's stopping cushion.

sec17-card-sec17-R08.question_text: Up to how far behind a large vehicle does its rear blind area reach, and what two views fail inside it?
sec17-card-sec17-R08.teaching_text: Tailgating a trailer blinds the trucker to your car while walling off your own sightline down the highway.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.question_text: Where should you position your car when following behind a large truck?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.teaching_text: Hanging far enough back to spot both west-coast mirrors lets the trucker track you and opens forward vision.

sec17-card-sec17-R10.question_text: Why does the handbook advise avoiding the right lane on steep hills and past truck weigh stations?
sec17-card-sec17-R10.teaching_text: Loaded rigs crawl around thirty-five on grades and reenter slowly from scales, creating huge speed gaps.

sec17-card-sec17-R11.question_text: Why must you give extra room to a truck or bus preparing for a right turn?
sec17-card-sec17-R11.teaching_text: Long trailer axles track inward, forcing cabs to swing wide left before rounding tight corners.

sec17-card-sec17-R12.question_text: Why must you never slip between the curb and a right-turning truck or bus?
sec17-card-sec17-R12.teaching_text: An open gap beside a left-swinging cab snaps shut as the trailer wheels cut across the curb.

sec17-card-sec17-R13.question_text: Where should you position your car when meeting an oncoming semi on a two-lane highway?
sec17-card-sec17-R13.teaching_text: Holding near the right edge adds clearance against bow-wave wind gusts and wide side mirrors.

sec17-card-sec17-R14.question_text: What should you do at a left turn if you cannot tell how fast an oncoming truck or bus is closing?
sec17-card-sec17-R14.teaching_text: Large silhouettes look deceptively slow from afar and cannot brake hard if you misjudge your turn.

sec17-card-sec17-R15.question_text: How does stopping behind painted white stop lines help large trucks and buses at intersections?
sec17-card-sec17-R15.teaching_text: Creeping past the white bar blocks the corner arc that fifty-foot trailers need to turn cleanly.

sec17-card-sec17-R16.question_text: Where must you never dart across a large vehicle's bow to make a sudden move?
sec17-card-sec17-R16.teaching_text: Slicing across a semi's front bumper for a missed exit or cone taper leaves zero room to stop.

sec17-card-sec17-R17.question_text: How must your speed behave when merging onto a highway ahead of a truck or bus?
sec17-card-sec17-R17.teaching_text: Pulling ahead of a heavy rig and then tapping brakes forces forty tons onto your rear bumper.

sec17-card-sec17-R18.question_text: Why does keeping a steady pace help a truck or bus starting from an acceleration lane?
sec17-card-sec17-R18.teaching_text: Predictable main-lane flow lets a slow-accelerating rig time one clean merge without stopping again.

sec17-card-sec17-R19.question_text: Why must you never stop or park on a runaway truck ramp or its approach?
sec17-card-sec17-R19.teaching_text: A smoking, brakeless semi barreling into gravel escape beds cannot steer around a parked family car.

sec17-card-sec17-R20.question_text: What visual sign warns of a runaway truck or bus, and how must you react?
sec17-card-sec17-R20.teaching_text: Billowing wheel smoke signals overheated, fading brakes, so get out of its lane and never pull ahead.

sec17-card-sec17-R21.question_text: What extra precaution applies around trucks and buses inside unmarked or shifting construction zones?
sec17-card-sec17-R21.teaching_text: Missing stripes and sudden flagger stops leave heavy rigs zero margin if a car darts in and brakes.

sec17-card-sec17-R22.question_text: How should you anticipate a transit bus making frequent curbside stops ahead?
sec17-card-sec17-R22.teaching_text: Changing lanes smoothly well upstream beats getting trapped right behind bumper-to-bumper bus stops.

sec17-card-sec17-R23.question_text: Which two sudden hazards must you watch for when easing past a parked transit bus?
sec17-card-sec17-R23.teaching_text: Disembarking riders often dash across the front bumper just as the bus signals back into traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-R24.question_text: About how far can the rear end of an articulated accordion bus swing sideways on turns?
sec17-card-sec17-R24.teaching_text: Crowding behind a hinged city bus puts your fender inside a three-foot rear overhang sweep.

sec17-card-sec17-R25.question_text: As vehicle size climbs, what happens to blind spots, stopping room, acceleration, and pass time?
sec17-card-sec17-R25.teaching_text: Every ton and foot of trailer expands blind zones and stretches every maneuver on the highway.

sec17-card-sec17-R26.question_text: How does driving a smaller vehicle affect whether truck and bus operators spot you?
sec17-card-sec17-R26.teaching_text: Low rooflines tuck completely below tall cab windows and hoodlines unless you hold extra distance.

sec17-card-sec17-R27.question_text: How must you yield to an approaching emergency vehicle running lights and siren?
sec17-card-sec17-R27.teaching_text: Clearing toward the right curb without blocking cross streets opens a clean corridor for responders.

sec17-card-sec17-R28.question_text: Where should you bring your car to a stop when signaled by a law-enforcement officer?
sec17-card-sec17-R28.teaching_text: Pulling promptly onto a firm right shoulder protects both the approaching officer and passing traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-R29.question_text: Should you step out of your car to meet the officer during a traffic stop?
sec17-card-sec17-R29.teaching_text: Stepping out unprompted looks threatening and exposes you to passing highway traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-R30.question_text: What engine, lighting, and window steps belong once pulled over for a police stop?
sec17-card-sec17-R30.teaching_text: Shutting down, flashing hazards, lighting a dark cabin, and lowering glass reassures the approaching officer.

sec17-card-sec17-R31.question_text: What should you and your passengers do with seat belts and hands while the officer walks up?
sec17-card-sec17-R31.teaching_text: Unbuckling or rummaging before the officer reaches your window looks like hiding items or preparing flight.

sec17-card-sec17-R32.question_text: Which three documents may be requested, and how should you reach for them safely?
sec17-card-sec17-R32.teaching_text: Telling the officer before reaching slowly with one hand on the wheel prevents dangerous misunderstandings.

sec17-card-sec17-R33.question_text: How should you respond to an officer's questions, and what choice must you never make?
sec17-card-sec17-R33.teaching_text: Calm answers keep roadside stops routine, whereas fleeing turns a ticket into a deadly felony pursuit.

sec17-card-sec17-R34.question_text: Below what travel speed does a rear orange-and-red reflective triangle indicate?
sec17-card-sec17-R34.teaching_text: Highway traffic at sixty-five closes on sub-twenty-five farm gear in mere seconds, demanding immediate braking.

sec17-card-sec17-R35.question_text: How should you approach and overtake slow-moving vehicles on the highway?
sec17-card-sec17-R35.teaching_text: Shedding speed early gives you time to check sightlines and wide implements before pulling out.

sec17-card-sec17-R36.question_text: What rural-road assumption must you avoid around tractors and farm equipment?
sec17-card-sec17-R36.teaching_text: Roaring diesel engines and enclosed cabs drown out approaching cars and horns completely.

sec17-card-sec17-R37.question_text: Do horseback riders and animal-drawn vehicles hold legal road rights and duties?
sec17-card-sec17-R37.teaching_text: Sharing rural lanes patiently respects their lawful right-of-way while keeping nervous animals calm.

sec17-card-sec17-R38.question_text: What two loud vehicle actions must you avoid near horses on or beside the road?
sec17-card-sec17-R38.teaching_text: Sudden horn blasts or exhaust roar can spook a thousand-pound horse right into your windshield.

sec17-card-sec17-R39.question_text: What sudden directional move should you anticipate from animal-drawn vehicles in farm country?
sec17-card-sec17-R39.teaching_text: Wagons and buggies lack electric blinkers and routinely swing left into farm lanes or pastures.

sec18-card-sec18-F01.question_text: Why is driving after dark inherently riskier than daytime driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F01.teaching_text: Outrunning your beam range leaves too little lit pavement to stop when dark obstacles appear.

sec18-card-sec18-F02.question_text: When should you run high beams at night versus switching down to low beams?
sec18-card-sec18-F02.teaching_text: Brights maximize open-road vision until oncoming windshields or preceding mirrors enter glare range.

sec18-card-sec18-F03.question_text: How should your beams and eyes respond when meeting oncoming headlights at night?
sec18-card-sec18-F03.teaching_text: Looking slightly toward the white fog stripe preserves night vision while keeping your lane centered.

sec18-card-sec18-F04.question_text: Why must you run low beams, plus fog lamps if equipped, in fog, rain, or falling snow?
sec18-card-sec18-F04.teaching_text: Upward high-beam rays bounce straight back off mist and flakes, shrinking how far you see.

sec18-card-sec18-F05.question_text: How should you manage your gaze when approaching headlights shine toward you?
sec18-card-sec18-F05.teaching_text: Staring straight into bright bulbs bleaches your retinas for seconds after the car passes.

sec18-card-sec18-F06.question_text: What visual clues ahead and along roadsides should your night scan search for?
sec18-card-sec18-F06.teaching_text: Unlit walkers, deer, and stalled cars show up first as dull silhouettes or edge movement.

sec18-card-sec18-F07.question_text: Why should you skip sunglasses or colored lenses at night and on overcast days?
sec18-card-sec18-F07.teaching_text: Any lens tint filters away scarce light and hides low-contrast hazards in gloom or darkness.

sec18-card-sec18-F08.question_text: At least how much time should you add to your normal following interval after dark?
sec18-card-sec18-F08.teaching_text: Darkness makes judging closing speed on red taillights harder, so stretching to five seconds buys margin.

sec18-card-sec18-F09.question_text: How many extra following seconds does the handbook call for at night on unfamiliar roads?
sec18-card-sec18-F09.teaching_text: Surprise curves, hills, and unmarked turns on strange roads demand two extra seconds of buffer.

sec18-card-sec18-F10.question_text: What three temporary traffic changes commonly appear inside a highway work zone?
sec18-card-sec18-F10.teaching_text: Expecting lane shifts and slow construction machinery keeps you alert before orange cones pinch traffic.

sec18-card-sec18-F11.question_text: Roughly how many injuries happen each year in vehicle crashes inside work zones?
sec18-card-sec18-F11.teaching_text: Drivers and passengers suffer alongside road crews when speeding cars slam into work-zone backups.

sec18-card-sec18-F12.question_text: What colors distinguish work-zone warning signs, and what hazards should you scan for ahead?
sec18-card-sec18-F12.teaching_text: Spotting diamond orange signs early cues you to scan for cones, heavy trucks, and workers.

sec18-card-sec18-F13.question_text: Why must you still slow down through a work zone even when no workers are on site?
sec18-card-sec18-F13.teaching_text: Concrete barriers, drop-offs, and milled asphalt stay hazardous long after crews clock out.

sec18-card-sec18-F14.question_text: What financial penalty warning accompanies posted speed limits inside work zones?
sec18-card-sec18-F14.teaching_text: Doubled citations enforce strict speed compliance where workers stand feet from rolling bumpers.

sec18-card-sec18-F15.question_text: Why should you read flashing digital boards alongside standard signs approaching roadwork?
sec18-card-sec18-F15.teaching_text: Electronic boards update in real time when sudden lane closures or stopped queues build ahead.

sec18-card-sec18-F16.question_text: What three driving adjustments belong all the way through an active work zone?
sec18-card-sec18-F16.teaching_text: Sudden flagger paddles and merging dump trucks punish drivers who tailgate through orange barrels.

sec18-card-sec18-F17.question_text: How should you treat driving through a work zone at night whether crews appear or not?
sec18-card-sec18-F17.teaching_text: Glare off reflective drums and shifted temporary stripes make nighttime lane edges tricky to read.

sec18-card-sec18-F18.question_text: How should you adjust lane position when passing road workers or construction rigs?
sec18-card-sec18-F18.teaching_text: Giving extra lateral space protects flaggers and crew members working inches past the cones.

sec18-card-sec18-F19.question_text: How far must you keep obeying work-zone limits and restrictions?
sec18-card-sec18-F19.teaching_text: Speeding up as soon as cones thin out risks tickets and crashes before the official end sign.

sec18-card-sec18-F20.question_text: What two trip-planning habits cut stress around scheduled road construction?
sec18-card-sec18-F20.teaching_text: Building buffer minutes or detouring around orange zones removes the urge to rush through cones.

sec18-card-sec18-R01.question_text: What three adjustments should kick in as soon as the season's first winter storm hits?
sec18-card-sec18-R01.teaching_text: Dry-summer muscle memory causes huge pileups during the first slick snowfall until drivers recalibrate.

sec18-card-sec18-R02.question_text: How should your speed and steering inputs change on snow-covered or icy winter roads?
sec18-card-sec18-R02.teaching_text: Posted signs show dry-pavement maximums, and sharp wheel jerks snap winter tire grip instantly.

sec18-card-sec18-R03.question_text: How does the winter-driving paragraph describe braking technique, and what system distinction does it omit there?
sec18-card-sec18-R03.teaching_text: Exam questions test that the winter section mentions gentle light pumping without separating anti-lock brakes there.

sec18-card-sec18-R04.question_text: What travel choices should you weigh before heading out in winter weather, including extreme storms?
sec18-card-sec18-R04.teaching_text: Skipping a nonessential trip in whiteout ice beats risking a stranded car on a frozen highway.

sec18-card-sec18-R05.question_text: May you run cruise control on wet, snowy, or icy roads?
sec18-card-sec18-R05.teaching_text: Cruise systems keep feeding power if tires spin on ice, turning a minor slip into a spinout.

sec18-card-sec18-R06.question_text: Which lights belong on in winter driving, and which setting should you skip in night snowstorms?
sec18-card-sec18-R06.teaching_text: Low beams make your car visible in blowing snow without blinding you in reflected flake glare.

sec18-card-sec18-R07.question_text: Does winter clothing or slow snow driving ever excuse skipping your seat belt?
sec18-card-sec18-R07.teaching_text: Slick-road spinouts and ditch rollovers happen at modest speeds where belts prevent ejection.

sec18-card-sec18-R08.question_text: Why must you slow down and give wide clearance to operating snowplows?
sec18-card-sec18-R08.teaching_text: Wing blades overhang lanes near the centerline while billowing snow plumes blind drivers close behind.

sec18-card-sec18-R09.question_text: How far back must you stay behind a flashing red-or-amber snowplow where the limit is thirty-five miles per hour or higher?
sec18-card-sec18-R09.teaching_text: Keeping at least two hundred feet clear gives you sightlines outside the plow's blinding snow wake.

sec18-card-sec18-R10.question_text: What three consequences can hit a driver who ignores closure gates and gets stuck on a closed road?
sec18-card-sec18-R10.teaching_text: Driving past storm gates risks waiting hours in subzero drifts plus paying citations and recovery costs.

sec18-card-sec18-R11.question_text: What three core habits keep you safe across open rural highways?
sec18-card-sec18-R11.teaching_text: Quiet country stretches lull drivers right before sharp bends, wildlife, or slow farm gear appear.

sec18-card-sec18-R12.question_text: How should you adjust speed and following gap when pavement turns to loose gravel or dirt?
sec18-card-sec18-R12.teaching_text: Loose stones roll like marbles beneath tires, cutting grip and skidding wheels under hard stops.

sec18-card-sec18-R13.question_text: How should you drive a narrow country road with steep drop-offs or almost no shoulder?
sec18-card-sec18-R13.teaching_text: Centering inside your lane avoids crumbling shoulder drop-offs while watching opposing cars crowding middle.

sec18-card-sec18-R14.question_text: How do drivers decide who crosses a narrow or single-lane rural bridge first?
sec18-card-sec18-R14.teaching_text: Yielding courteously so the vehicle reaching the bridge first clears prevents head-on deck standoffs.

sec18-card-sec18-R15.question_text: What three steps belong on open-grate or steel rural bridge decks?
sec18-card-sec18-R15.teaching_text: Wet steel grates wander slightly under tire treads and offer far less stopping friction than asphalt.

sec18-card-sec18-R16.question_text: How must you drive where tall corn, timber, blind bends, or steep crests block rural visibility?
sec18-card-sec18-R16.teaching_text: Summer crops and steep hills hide tractors, deer, and cross traffic until seconds before impact.

sec18-card-sec18-R17.question_text: How should you approach an uncontrolled rural intersection with no signs or lights?
sec18-card-sec18-R17.teaching_text: Gravel crossroads often lack stop signs entirely, so easing off early prevents high-speed T-bone crashes.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Why must you evaluate live traffic conditions instead of assuming right-of-way rules guarantee your path?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Right-of-way laws assign yielding duties, yet insisting on priority when another car fails to stop still causes a crash.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: How do you yield when another driver is already in an intersection or gets there ahead of you?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Letting vehicles that arrived or entered ahead of you clear first prevents T-bone collisions at intersections.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Who gets priority when you want to turn left across an opposing lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Cutting left across the path of straight oncoming traffic is one of the top causes of severe intersection wrecks.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: Who yields when two drivers reach an all-way stop at the exact same time?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Giving priority to the vehicle on your right breaks simultaneous all-way ties smoothly without guesswork.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Who must yield when a vehicle pulls onto a public highway from a private road or driveway?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Through vehicles cruising at highway speed expect private-driveway and alley traffic to wait for a wide, safe gap.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Who has the duty to yield where an entrance or acceleration ramp meets an interstate highway?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Drivers already established on limited-access lanes hold priority, so ramp drivers adjust speed to blend into open gaps.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: Which three groups still inside an intersection must receive right-of-way before you enter?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Even when your light turns green, anyone still clearing the box on foot, two wheels, or four wheels goes first.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Which vehicle in a South Dakota funeral procession must obey traffic signs and signals?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Once the lead vehicle lawfully enters on a green or clear stop, trailing procession cars stay together as one unit.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: How do funeral-procession cars mark themselves, and what must surrounding motorists avoid doing?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Lit headlights identify the continuous funeral line so other drivers wait patiently instead of wedging between cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Besides signs, signals, and lane paint, which three groups of people direct traffic as official controls?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Hand directions from law enforcement, highway flaggers, and school crossing guards carry binding traffic-control authority.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: Where are pedestrian hybrid beacons installed to help walkers cross safely?
