sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Wide, fast streets without full traffic lights use hybrid beacons to halt vehicles on demand for crossing walkers.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: How many red and yellow lenses make up the pedestrian hybrid beacon described in the handbook?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Unlike standard three-color traffic heads, a hybrid beacon arranges two side-by-side red lamps above one bottom yellow lamp.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: How does a pedestrian hybrid beacon appear before a walker presses the crossing button?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Unlike a power-out intersection light, a hybrid beacon intentionally stays dark until a pedestrian triggers it.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What color progression directs motorists to slow and stop once a pedestrian activates a hybrid beacon?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Flashing then steady yellow warns traffic to slow before solid and alternating red lights command a full stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What happens on the pedestrian screen and overhead beacon as the walker finishes crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Once pedestrians cross during the walk display and clear the street, the overhead beacon shuts dark for flowing traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: How are red, yellow, and green lenses ordered on vertical versus horizontal traffic signals?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Standard lens positions let color-vision-deficient drivers read red at the top or far left every single time.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: What must you wait for at a steady red light before driving straight through?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Wait at a full stop until green appears and any lingering cross-street vehicles finish clearing.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Under what three conditions may you make a right turn at a steady red light?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Rolling through a red right turn or ignoring a posted no-turn-on-red sign earns a red-light ticket.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Who gets right-of-way before you turn on red, and where must your car finish the turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Yield to walkers, cyclists, and cross cars first, then turn cleanly into the proper near lane without swinging wide.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: Which intersection sign matches the exact rule for a flashing red traffic light?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Come to a complete halt, check cross traffic and crosswalks, and proceed only when your path is clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: When may you move in the direction pointed by a steady red arrow?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red light where right-on-red may apply, a steady red arrow forbids turning until green appears.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: What does a steady yellow traffic light warn, and what action does it require?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Speeding up to beat a yellow light invites high-speed T-bone crashes with cross traffic launching on green.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: What should you do if the signal switches to yellow after your car is already inside the intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Slamming brakes or reversing inside the box leaves your vehicle stranded directly across cross-street lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: How should you drive through an intersection displaying a flashing yellow light?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Flashing yellow marks heightened cross-street or hazard risk without requiring a full stop unless traffic conflicts.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: What does a steady yellow arrow warn turning drivers to do?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Your dedicated left-turn phase is wrapping up, meaning opposing cars are about to gain straight-ahead priority.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: What must you do before turning left on a flashing yellow left arrow?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: A flashing yellow arrow allows permissive left turns only after both oncoming cars and crosswalk walkers clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: What signal color is oncoming traffic facing while you see a flashing yellow left arrow?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Never assume oncoming cars are stopping, because their steady green gives them full straight-ahead priority.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: Does a steady green light erase your duty to yield to emergency vehicles or legally protected road users?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Green grants permission to go only after sirens, crosswalk users, and intersection-clearing vehicles are safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: What must clear out of the intersection when your red light first turns green?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Launching the instant green illuminates without scanning left and right risks getting hit by a red-light runner.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: Under what rules may you turn left at a steady circular green signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Without a green arrow, straight oncoming traffic goes first and any posted left-turn ban still applies.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: Who must you watch closely across your path during any left or right turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Parallel walk signals often run alongside green traffic phases, placing pedestrians directly across your turning lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: What traffic condition is expected when a steady green arrow illuminates for your turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: A green arrow holds opposing and cross streams on red, though defensive drivers still scan before turning.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: How should a driver facing green proceed when a traffic signal is malfunctioning under South Dakota statute?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: If a glitching signal shows green on your approach, creep forward with high caution rather than blasting through.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: How should a driver facing yellow proceed at a malfunctioning traffic signal under South Dakota statute?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Stuck or malfunctioning yellow indications call for slow, watchful movement prepared to yield to cross traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: How must you treat a malfunctioning signal that is stuck red or completely dark?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: During blackouts or stuck-red faults, treating the intersection like an all-way stop prevents high-speed cross collisions.
sec09-card-sec09-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Treat dark or red as stop

visual_sync.text_span: Treat dark or red as stop

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Which four visual features help you recognize a road sign's category from a distance?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Distinct shapes and colors let you read a sign's message through snow, glare, or distance before reading small text.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: What standard shape and color scheme identify most roadway warning signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Spotting a yellow diamond ahead cues you immediately to scan for curves, merges, or surface changes.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: Which three pedestrian-focused warning zones often use bright fluorescent yellow signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: High-visibility fluorescent yellow-green stands out sharply at dawn and dusk around children and foot crossings.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: What do warning signs announce, and how should your driving adjust?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Easing off the gas and covering the brake early turns a hidden curve or crossing into a routine pass.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: What shape and markings warn in advance of a railroad crossing, and what four actions follow?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Round yellow advance signs with black crossing letters tell you to slow down, look both ways, listen, and prepare to stop.
sec09-card-sec09-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Round yellow sign, slow, look, listen

visual_sync.text_span: Round yellow sign, slow, look, listen

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: What white X-shaped sign stands right beside the tracks at a highway-rail crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: A white crossbuck marks the exact track location and carries the same legal duty to yield as a yield sign.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Where must you stop at a crossbuck crossing when a train or rail vehicle approaches?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Locomotives overhang wider than the steel rails, so stay well behind the painted stop line until tracks clear completely.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: What hidden danger does a multiple-track sign warn about below a crossbuck?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Pulling out right behind the caboose of train one can put you directly in front of a fast train on track two.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: Why must you scan carefully for extra tracks and trains at every rail crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Rural crossings may have zero flashing lights or track-count plaques, making your own eyes and ears vital.
sec09-card-sec09-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Some crossings lack signs or lights

visual_sync.text_span: Some crossings lack signs or lights

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: What action is mandatory whenever rail-crossing red lights flash alternately?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Alternating red crossing flashers mean a train is closing fast and crossing the rails is strictly illegal.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: May you ever weave around a lowered railroad crossing gate if no train is visible?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Trains travel much faster than they look, making gate-weaving both unlawful and frequently fatal.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: When a railroad crossing bell or horn is sounding, when is it lawful to cross?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Active crossing bells warn that rail equipment is still approaching or occupying the crossing zone.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: What vital contact information appears on the railroad Emergency Notification System sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: Calling the railroad's direct emergency line alerts train dispatchers far faster than general calls when a vehicle stalls on rails.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: What color sign displays the emergency notification phone number at a railroad crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Look for the rectangular blue placard mounted on the crossbuck post or signal cabinet right beside the tracks.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: What does the Department of Transportation code on the blue railroad sign identify?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Six digits and a letter pinpoint that exact rural or city track crossing when street addresses do not exist.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: Why must you read off the Department of Transportation crossing identifier when calling railroad dispatch?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Giving the exact crossing code lets dispatchers radio engineers on that line immediately to slow or halt trains.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.question_text: What color and shapes distinguish temporary work-zone signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.teaching_text: Bright orange backgrounds with black symbols instantly signal temporary construction, maintenance, or utility activity ahead.
sec09-card-sec09-R17.must_match_memory_hook: Orange diamonds or rectangles, black print

visual_sync.text_span: Orange diamonds or rectangles, black print

sec09-card-sec09-R18.question_text: Which five roadway changes do orange work-zone signs commonly announce?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.teaching_text: Uneven milled pavement, slow dump trucks, lane detours, and crews standing feet from traffic demand immediate speed drops.
sec09-card-sec09-R18.must_match_memory_hook: Workers, lower speeds, detours, gear, surfaces

visual_sync.text_span: Workers, lower speeds, detours, gear, surfaces

sec09-card-sec09-R19.question_text: How must you respond to a work-zone flagger's paddle sign or flag directions?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.teaching_text: Flaggers coordinate one-lane alternating traffic around blind equipment where ignoring a paddle causes head-on collisions.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.question_text: What job do orange drums, cones, vertical panels, and barricades perform in a work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.teaching_text: Channelizing lines steer vehicles smoothly around open trenches, wet concrete, and workers.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.question_text: Where must you halt when stopping for a temporary portable traffic signal in a work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.teaching_text: Stopping behind the painted or taped white bar leaves wide turning clearance for opposing trucks on single-lane detours.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.question_text: What three driving adjustments keep you crash-free through an active work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.teaching_text: Rear-end collisions lead all work-zone crashes, so generous following space and lower speed save lives.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.question_text: What happens to speeding fines inside a South Dakota highway work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.teaching_text: Doubled citations reinforce how dangerous excess speed is when workers stand inches from live lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R24.question_text: What types of enforceable rules do regulatory signs communicate?
sec09-card-sec09-R24.teaching_text: Unlike advisory warnings, regulatory signs state traffic laws for speed, turns, lanes, direction, and parking that carry tickets.
sec09-card-sec09-R24.must_match_memory_hook: Enforceable speed, turn, lane, parking laws

visual_sync.text_span: Enforceable speed, turn, lane, parking laws

sec09-card-sec09-R25.question_text: What background color, marking colors, and shapes characterize regulatory signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R25.teaching_text: Most regulatory signs use crisp white squares or vertical rectangles, plus special shapes like octagons and triangles.

sec09-card-sec09-R26.question_text: What does a red circle with a diagonal slash drawn across a black symbol mean?
sec09-card-sec09-R26.teaching_text: Universal red-circle-and-slash symbols ban U-turns, left turns, trucks, or bicycles at a single glance.

sec09-card-sec09-R27.question_text: Which two speed boundaries can black-and-white regulatory speed signs establish?
sec09-card-sec09-R27.teaching_text: Highways sometimes pair a top legal speed limit with a minimum pace so slow traffic does not block fast lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R28.question_text: When is driving the full posted maximum speed appropriate, and when must you drop below it?
sec09-card-sec09-R28.teaching_text: Rain, snow, glare, fog, or icy patches require dropping well below the dry-weather sign number.

sec09-card-sec09-R29.question_text: What should you do if conditions or your vehicle keep you from safely matching a road's posted minimum speed?
sec09-card-sec09-R29.teaching_text: Creeping below an interstate minimum creates severe rear-end closing speeds, so switch to a secondary route.

sec09-card-sec09-R30.question_text: What unique shape and color combination belongs exclusively to a stop sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R30.teaching_text: Even from the back or covered in frost, an eight-sided octagon silhouette unmistakably means stop.

sec09-card-sec09-R31.question_text: In South Dakota's regulatory sign rules, where do you stop at a stop sign and what follows?
sec09-card-sec09-R31.teaching_text: Rolling past the painted limit bar or pedestrian lane forces walkers into live cross-street lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R32.question_text: What shape, orientation, and colors identify a standard yield sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R32.teaching_text: No other traffic sign uses a downward-pointing triangle, letting you spot yield priority from either side.

sec09-card-sec09-R33.question_text: What must you do as you approach a yield sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R33.teaching_text: Slow enough to stop if needed and let vehicles or pedestrians in the road you are entering go first.

sec09-card-sec09-R34.question_text: How must you travel when entering or driving along a street marked with one-way signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R34.teaching_text: Turning against a one-way arrow puts you nose-to-nose with every lane of oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R35.question_text: How do roads mark where legal passing starts, ends, or stays off-limits?
sec09-card-sec09-R35.teaching_text: Pennant signs, rectangular regulatory signs, and solid yellow centerlines work together to mark no-passing boundaries.

sec09-card-sec09-R36.question_text: What sightline factors and hidden features determine where engineers place no-passing zones?
sec09-card-sec09-R36.teaching_text: Even when a road looks calm, dips, curves, intersections, and driveways can pop a car into the oncoming lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R37.question_text: Does a broken yellow passing zone mean it is automatically safe to pull out and overtake?
sec09-card-sec09-R37.teaching_text: Broken paint only says passing is legal in clear conditions; oncoming traffic, rain, or glare still require staying back.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: What must you scan at every corner and activate before starting a turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Checking signs, walkers, and cars across all four corners prevents mid-turn surprises.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: Which lane position should you enter and hold when preparing to turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Moving to the curb side for right turns or center side for left turns blocks cars from squeezing inside.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: How far along your intended turning path should you aim your eyes?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Scanning well into the cross street spots jaywalkers or stopped bumpers before your nose swings around.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: What three steps finish a turn cleanly once your wheels straighten?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Matching street pace, confirming your blinker clicked off, and checking behind blends you smoothly into traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: From where in your lane do you start a right turn, and what steering habit must you avoid?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Swinging wide left before turning right tricks drivers into thinking you are changing lanes left.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: Where in your lane do you begin a left turn, and who holds priority?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Hugging the left lane edge clears passing room behind you while you wait for oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: How must you handle lane selection when two or more lanes turn together?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Drifting across dotted turn guides mid-corner clips the vehicle turning right beside your fender.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: How does a two-point turnabout reverse your direction when circling the block isn't practical?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Pulling or backing briefly into a side driveway avoids blocking both lanes sideways across the road.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What three initial actions start a reverse two-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Signaling right and halting past the driveway lets trailing cars understand and clear before you back.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: When do you turn the steering wheel fully right while backing into a reverse two-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Aligning your rear bumper with the near apron edge swings the tail cleanly inside without hopping curbs.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: What do you do with steering and brakes once your car backs into the driveway?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Square front tires set up a clean forward pullout once cross traffic clears.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: How do you complete a reverse two-point turnabout from inside the driveway?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Backing into the driveway first lets you finish with a high-visibility forward left turn into traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: How do you position and signal to start a forward two-point turnabout into a left driveway?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Approaching near road center and entering the driveway's right side leaves room to swing back out.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: Where do you stop inside the driveway during a forward two-point turnabout before shifting to Reverse?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Pulling just far enough for your rear bumper to clear the street preps an all-around check and right signal.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: How do you steer, shift, and finish backing out of a forward two-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Backing slowly right into the nearest lane avoids swinging wide across opposing traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: When is a three-point turnabout appropriate to use?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Because a three-point turn blocks both lanes sideways, save it strictly for narrow two-lanes lacking alternatives.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: What three steps begin a three-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Pulling fully against the right edge opens maximum turning width across the narrow two-lane road.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: How do you execute the first forward crossing of a three-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Checking left blind spots before cranking sharply left prevents turning across an overtaking car.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: How do you perform the middle reversing stage of a three-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Scanning both blind spots while turning sharply right positions your nose toward your new travel lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: What checks and signals accompany the final forward turn of a three-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Re-checking both directions before turning left puts you cleanly into the right-hand lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: What final checks follow completing a three-point turnabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Verifying traffic behind and a canceled turn signal lets you accelerate straight without misleading followers.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: How does a U-turn reverse your direction compared with multi-point turnabouts?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Wide pavement lets a vehicle swing around in one continuous arc without stopping to reverse.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: When may you make a U-turn at an intersection directed by a police officer?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Unexpected U-turns snarl manual traffic flow unless the directing officer specifically waves you around.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: Where are midblock U-turns prohibited in South Dakota, and what divided-road exception exists?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Turning midblock snarls storefronts and through streets unless using a lawful divided-highway crossover.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: May you make a U-turn where a No U-Turn regulatory sign is posted?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Posted bans mark tight turning geometry, heavy pedestrian crossings, or fast signal phases.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: What minimum sight distance from all directions is required for a U-turn near a curve or hillcrest on an undivided highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Swinging across an undivided highway inside five hundred feet of a blind crest invites high-speed broadsides.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: What general safety test governs every otherwise legal U-turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Even where unposted, forcing oncoming or trailing vehicles to brake makes a U-turn unlawful.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: What speed adjustment and six visual checks apply as you approach an intersection?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Easing speed gives your eyes time to read signals, cross traffic, walkers, cyclists, pavement, and blind corners.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: Why shouldn't you count on cross-street drivers obeying signs, signals, or yield rules?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Distracted drivers blow through red lights and stop signs daily, making crash readiness essential.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: What scanning sequence should you use for cross traffic and bicycles after stopping at an intersection?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Checking left a second time catches fast traffic in the first lane you are about to cross.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: Why shouldn't you floor the gas the instant a red light turns green?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Late yellow-runners or pedestrians finishing a crossing may still occupy the intersection box.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: How big must your traffic gap be when crossing or turning onto a cross street?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Counting on fast cross-traffic to brake for your slow pullout causes rear-end and T-bone crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: Why shouldn't you pull out solely because an approaching car has its turn signal flashing?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: The approaching driver might aim for a driveway beyond you or have forgotten an earlier blinker.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: Which way does traffic circulate inside a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Bearing right on entry keeps every vehicle inside the circle orbiting counterclockwise.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: By roughly what percentages do roundabouts cut fatal crashes, injury crashes, and total crashes?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Eliminating high-speed left crosses and red-light T-bones slashes fatal intersection wrecks by roughly ninety percent.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: What is a roundabout's inner truck apron built for, and which vehicles must stay off it?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Raised inner pavement lets long semitrailers track around tight circles while passenger cars stay in lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How should you manage speed, signs, walkers, and cyclists when approaching a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Low entry speed lets you read lane arrows and stop cleanly for crosswalk users.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Which direction do you check for priority vehicles before entering a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Because roundabout traffic orbits counterclockwise, priority vehicles always approach from your left.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: What speed rule applies while driving inside a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Calm circular pace prevents side-slip and gives smooth room for nearby entries and exits.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: What signal and yield duties apply as your roundabout exit approaches?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Right blinkers inform waiting drivers while yielding protects pedestrians and cyclists crossing the exit leg.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: Who always holds priority when emergency sirens approach a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Fire trucks, ambulances, and patrol units need unobstructed passage through circular intersections.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches before you enter a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Pulling right on the approach leg keeps the narrow curved roadway open for wide rescue rigs.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already circulating inside a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Stopping inside a curved single or dual lane chokes off the exact path the ambulance needs.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: How do you choose the proper lane before entering a multilane roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Picking your lane before the yield line avoids illegal lane changes inside spiral markings.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: Which lane is generally used to turn left at a multilane roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Starting left turns from an unmarked right outer lane cuts directly across through-moving inner cars.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: Which lane is generally used to turn right at a multilane roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Using the outer right lane or a marked right-turn lane lets you peel off cleanly at exit one.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: Which lane should you pick when continuing straight through a multilane roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Depending on site layout, one or both entry lanes may carry straight arrows, so signs govern.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: What traffic movements require special attention at a cloverleaf highway interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Curved loop ramps feed merging cars right beside drivers slowing to exit.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: What conflict happens inside cloverleaf weaving sections between loop ramps?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: Drivers accelerating onto the freeway share the same short auxiliary lane with drivers slowing to exit.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: Why must you shed substantial speed on cloverleaf loop ramps?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: Carrying freeway momentum into a tight two-hundred-seventy-degree loop risks skidding or rolling.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: Which three interchange designs avoid cloverleaf weaving conflicts?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: Signalized ramp terminals separate entering and exiting streams instead of mixing them on short loops.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: Do ordinary intersection traffic rules still apply inside a diverging-diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Even though lanes cross temporarily left, familiar signals, lane stripes, and yield rules guide every step.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: How should you navigate the first signalized crossover of a diverging-diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: Guided curbing and lane paint channel your side smoothly across so travel feels like a one-way street.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.question_text: Why are left turns onto the freeway effortless inside a diverging-diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.teaching_text: Because crossover lanes already ride on the left, freeway left-turners peel onto ramps without crossing oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.question_text: What does a driver traveling straight across a diverging-diamond interchange encounter at the far end?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.teaching_text: A second coordinated signal shifts straight-through traffic smoothly back onto the right-hand side.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.question_text: Where must pedestrians walk and cross inside a diverging-diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.teaching_text: Angled vehicle crossovers shift traffic directions, so sticking to marked walkways and crosswalks keeps walkers protected.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.question_text: Which two routing options may bicyclists use through a diverging-diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.teaching_text: Cyclists can either follow the marked bike lane or use designated pedestrian walkways and crosswalks.

sec11-card-sec11-R22.question_text: May a motorist drive across an interstate highway's center median?
sec11-card-sec11-R22.teaching_text: Paved emergency turnarounds exist strictly for patrol and rescue units, never civilian U-turns.

sec11-card-sec11-R23.question_text: What must you do if you overshoot your intended exit on an interstate?
sec11-card-sec11-R23.teaching_text: Backing along a freeway shoulder or lane puts reverse speed head-on into seventy-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R24.question_text: Which interstate lane habit applies when you are not overtaking slower traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-R24.teaching_text: Keeping right except to pass leaves the left lane open and reduces blind-spot conflicts.

sec11-card-sec11-R25.question_text: How should you manage your cruising pace on an interstate highway?
sec11-card-sec11-R25.teaching_text: Matching smooth freeway flow without exceeding posted signs prevents accordion braking and passing conflicts.
